text: We decided to try the new Texas Roadhouse last night, their website gave a number to call for reservations..ooops..when I called they said they don't take reservations, that I can call an hour early and get on the list, which I did. When we arrived we only had to wait 10 minutes or so, but I am not sure we would have had to wait any longer had I not called ahead. Sadly, I developed a negative opinion of this place before I ever tried the food, I got really irritated when I spotted the large sign on the wall: "We do not seat incomplete parties". I was like WTF??? My husband frequently drops me off in front of restaurants to get a table while he parks, I never even considered that it might offend a restaurant manager, all I can figure is that Texas Roadhouse is so convinced that they will remain packed with waiting lines that they think they can turn away customers who might want to be seated prior to the arrival of one of their party. (Too bad they don't know that in Reno everything new is packed, remember Krispy Kreme with the hour long lines? lol) I have to commend their attention to service, our server was attentive, prompt and friendly, her manager stopped at the table twice to ask us how things were going. The food gets mixed reviews, my husband ordered the rib eye and proclaimed that it was the best steak he has ever had in Reno. He was less impressed by the vegetable side which consisted of carrots and broccoli served steamed with no seasoning (reminds me of the veggies in any one of the cheap casino coffee shops). He didn't care for the baked potato which appeared to be deep fried, that seems to be gaining popularity but neither of us care for it. I ordered the "fall of the bone" ribs and they do indeed fall off the bone, but that is their only redeeming quality, the outside was badly charred, and the sauce was no better than any one of a dozen you might pick up on a grocery store shelf. For my side dishes I ordered a cup of chili and fries. The chili was brought to me before my entree, I'm not sure why they did that, i would have preferred it with my meal. The chili was ok, but rather bland, and the fries were nice. Bottom line, I just can't see myself going back there, I prefer Ruby River, at least there you can have a conversation at your table without screaming over 'too loud' country music.

text: I've waited over 2 years to write this review. Why? Because I know how much of a Yelp favorite this salon is and I wanted to see if I was still bitter over my god-awful haircut from there. Guess what - I am. When I first moved to Philadelphia, I was still going to home to Delaware to my regular salon because I'm very faithful to my stylists. Unfortunately, it became increasingly hard to do that since I was relying on my parents and sister for rides. After talking to several co-workers, I was convinced that while this place was expensive, it could be well-worth the money for a cut/dye. Plus, I was told there was some kind of Sunday promotion at the time for half-off hair cuts or whatever which definitely sweetened the deal. Basically things just went wrong from there. The salon itself is SUPER hip and chic. I felt like I was hanging out in SoHo instead of Sansom Street. The staff was nice enough once I got past the front desk, and the girl who did my dye job actually did a fantastic job (the only reason this place is getting two stars). I've actually debated going back to this place for the dye job alone, but really it's just not worth the money. Now, in terms of my hair cut? I went in there with a general idea of what I wanted. I have curly hair so I have a hard time being adventurous, but I told my stylist (her name was Jen or Liz or some other monosyllabic name, I believe) that I wanted something modern that I could wear both curly and straight. She said she could definitely do that but would probably need to take about 1-1 1/2 inches off. I was completely fine with that and expected it because my hair hadn't been cut in awhile. What she COMPLETELY neglected to tell me is that she was going to take about 6-7 inches off my top layers, which, for those of you that don't have curly hair, looks like a lot more. By the time she had begun doing that, it was too late to say anything because it's not like I was going to leave with one section of ridiculously short layers. As I forced through the conversation and faked how much I "liked" my new haircut, it was all I could do to fight the tears. Then, to top everything off, I was slapped with a $120 bill. Again, I expected something that expensive but remember when I was told that they had a Sunday promotion? Yeah, I never got that. I have no idea why. I'm going to be perfectly honest when I say that this was BY FAR the worst haircut I've ever had and I cried over it for 3 days, which is saying a lot because I generally don't care about cuts that much. This whole experience scarred me so much that I waited 8 months to get my hair cut again, and I only did because I went home to Delaware to my original salon. After that, I waited another year to even consider getting my hair cut again in Philadelphia. I know this place gets stellar reviews, but please. Just be wary.

text: Went to the buffet twice...once on a Monday, when it was 16.99, and the 2nd time on a Friday, when it was "sea food" themed (no lobsters) and cost me 25.99 per person. Two were the same!! Prime ribs are nice and juicy, but much like all NV buffets, they were a bit over cooked and they only slice you a paper thin slice every time you go up to the carving station. Of course you could ask for a 2nd slice.. but it doesn't feel the same. King crab legs are WAY TOO SALTY. This seems like the things Reno buffets do: have high dollar value items, but make them hard to eat. I love crabs and I have a very high sodium tolerance. But man, even I couldn't eat too much of those king crab legs! On a side note: I saw some of the smallest king crab legs there ever! They are either a different specie/grade of king crabs, or they are buying under sized king crabs. Snow crab legs were pretty good. Decent size too. The best part is that they do serve some of them hot! Which made it a lot easier to eat. Raw oysters on sea food night: It didn't feel right. Felt like oysters rinsed with chemicals to preserve shelf life. Those things had a distinctive bitter taste to them and in general, don't taste like fresh oysters. (You don't even get a not-fresh oyster taste.) Ever seen that white milky color liquid they use to preserve scallops on processing boats? My guess is that those oysters went through similar treatment so they have a longer "buffet life". Everything else was average. Mexican section was pretty good. Asian station had VERY limited choices. And I have no I idea why somehow people liked their desert. I am a big cake fan. But the cakes there were nothing but sugar, flour, and Veggie Oil. Yes, Veggie oil. Much like the cake you get from crappy super markets. They are lower in cost and lasts longer. After you eat their cake or fruit tarts, you will feel a coat of grease on your lip and tongue. That is because hydronated vegetable oil has a higher melting point than cream, and your body temperature is not hot enough to melt them away. Didn't try their cookies, as I didn't think it was appropriate to eat cookies after I paid all that much money for the buffet. Bottom line is: 16.99, give a try. 25.99, STAY AWAY!!!!!!!!

text: To the owners of monkey burger: PLEASE take to heart the reviews about your service. It is unbelievably, ridiculously terrible. My first choice for you is no stars. Well, the first time I visited, it was only bad. It was the second visit where our entire evening experience and conversation were hijacked by our stupified disbelief about how a restaurant could stay open while disregarding the most simple basic pieces of operation. First vist: I met a friend for lunch. It was busy, but one server was very sweet and attentive to the fact i had my infant with me, opening the front door and then bringing a high chair and turning it over to show me how to fit the car seat securely between the chair legs. Please, monkeyburger - make him employee of the year immediately. Better yet, fire the entire rest of your staff and start over. The short of it: We placed our orders and had to inquire twice about our drinks before they arrived. I had to get up for a refill on water as no one was checking our table while we ate.. Once food came, the server offered to bring us ketchup and mustard but then disappeared. The burgers we ordered medium but arrived definitely medium rare, with bright red, uncooked middle. The food looked great, but tasted just pretty good - lacking in flavor somehow which is pretty tough to achieve with a burger with so many toppings. Despite this experience, I suggested a couple of weeks later to my husband and brother-in-law that we go for dinner on a thursday night. We arrived around 7:00, it was pretty full, most everyone was finishing up and leaving. The place was dim as the overhead lights were off and the 80's easy listening playing was in very weird contrast to the graffiti style walls. THe guy at the cash register who took our orders didn't greet us as we stook only 3 feet from him ready to order, couldn't make eye contact nor string two words together to answer our questions about the menu - I wanted to know how they defined "medium" and "medium rare" having gotten what I considered an undercooked burger the first time. It wasn't so much that he had attitude, just seemed like he was honestly incapable of customer service. Like my previous experience, we had to ask twice about our drinks before the guy at the register took the 30 seconds to open up three bottles. We had to repeat what drinks we wanted for him three times. If we hadn't been thirsty, it would have been comical. The burgers arrived a solid 40 minutes after we'd ordered with not a single pass from a server to refill waters or let us know what was going on (the restaurant was not busy at this time - it had emptied since we arrived). The answers about how they cooked their meat had done nothing to reassure me I'd get what I wanted so I ordered a turkey burger. Again, it was pretty good not great. My husband had ordered his burger cooked medium well and it was bright red raw in the middle. We encouraged him to send it back, despite the fact it was totally late and we were ready to get out of there. His brother's burger was also undercooked but he just decided to deal with it. About 10 minutes later, the retry on the medium well came back, my husband took a bite and it was cooked EXACTLY like the first one had been - medium rare to rare. No one came back to inquire about the burger so I got up, and requested a refund for the meal as he was not interested in waiting for a third redo. We were given instead a punchcard for a free burger - not helpful as there are plenty of other places in town to get a better tasting burger with great service. While we were there, someone who i suspect may have been the owner or manager showed up and we overheard him speaking with a table who were also complaining about the food and service. He also had words with the cash register guy about the lights and then generally stalked around the restaurant and in and out of the kitchen looking pissed off for about 10 minutes. Monkey Burger: fooled me once, shame on you. fooled me twice, shame on me... And I certainly won't be back to be made a fool of again.

text: Okay, I can only comment on the breakfast and tour as opposed to the Bed and Breakfast portion of this fine establishment. The in-laws were coming into town and LivingSocial put up a deal for half-price breakfasts and tours for the Degas House. My husband thought it'd be a nice thing to do with his parents so I picked up the vouchers for the group. Initially, we were a tad confused as to where we were supposed to go when we first got there. We weren't familiar with the Degas House and we didn't realize it was two buildings (though there's a whole story where it used to be one building). After wandering around for a bit, we figured out where the office was and got little bands around our wrists to show we were there for the tour and breakfast. We had the choice to go on the tour or have breakfast first; we decided to have breakfast first. It's a really casual place so we sat at whatever table we wanted and a lady came and gave us a menu. The menu gives you three choices in what type of breakfast you want; waffles, french toast, or an omelet. Then you get to choose whatever else you want with to go with the main dish; eggs, grits, bacon, bread, etc. The breakfast was absolutely divine. Portions were huge and everything was so tasty. You also get a free drink, either a Bloody Mary or a Mimosa. Warning! The Bloody Mary is very strong! On top of the breakfast menu, there are a ton of pastries you can snack on. The tour was fine, but the in-laws weren't feeling very patient. First, there's a video which is too long and then you get a tour of the buildings. It's all very interesting but on the web site it says the tour is an hour long, and we left early after the tour went on for an hour and a half. With the breakfast and the tour, we were at the Degas Hour for almost four hours and the in-laws were ready to see the rest of the city. I think it would have been better for us to have the tour and then breakfast. It was definitely worth it with the awesome breakfast. :) NOM!

text: Not counting the years I didn't live in Nashville after college, I have been going to Maryland Farms since the days of the Maryland Farms Country Club. Now, it is a YMCA. The YMCA at Maryland Farms is extremely spacious and houses some very nice perks. The free weight area (which I use the most) has 4 bench presses, 4 squat machines, a decline bench, an incline bench, a leg press (with 100lbs. weights available, which is nice not to have to stack like six 45lbs. weights to do a decent press), and a row. There are, of course, every imaginable weight machine available as well from chest fly to thigh machines. The dumbbell area has dumbbells ranging from 2.5lbs. to 120lbs. and there are plenty of chairs and adjustable benches upon which to do anything from preacher curls to shoulder presses to dumbbell bench (flat, decline, or incline). Needless to say the weights section has something for the first-timer and something for the meatheads. The cardio machine area has ellipticals, treadmills, two machines that simulate rollerblading/skating, stairsteps and the like. The machines are newer machines with touchscreen technology that allows for docking an iPod to watching any of 65+ channels of TV while you run/walk/skate your cardio away. The spin classes run solely in the mornings, so if you're into spin then you'd better be into working out in the AM. Spin classes have start times from 5:15AM every hour until 9:15AM. Additionally, there is a movie theater room where you can do cardio (again on the same machines mentioned in the previous paragraph) but watch a digital projector 101+inch screen of a movie that is listed. They post the family-friendly movies for the next week each month. There is an Olympic sized indoor swimming pool and 3 or 4 indoor tennis courts. There are two large pools with slides and such outside accompanied by even more outdoor tennis courts. It's like belonging to a country club without the country club dues... of course, there also is not a golf course. It's a great YMCA.

text: Disclosure: I am a recovering Tucsonan now well-settled in Phoenix. I enjoy the Phoenix-area nightlife, and that does occasionally include the douchebaggy, cheesy Scottsdale club scene (you know, my city right or wrong). I guess it has its role to play, so I wish it no harm, I don't (deliberately) judge those who partake in it, and I even indulge myself from time to time when I'm with friends who leave me no other options. But none of that excuses the severe dose of lameness that Level pukes on to the Tucson scene (more on puking later), which I discovered for the first time on a recent weekend trip to see some old friends. Level is aptly named, because it somehow elevates Tucson's nightlife to a whole new level of the wannabe-syndrome. Simply put, Level is wannabe-Scottsdale which is in turn wannabe-LA. Once I was finally allowed in by the thugs jealously guarding the place to give it an artificial aura of exclusivity, I looked around and basically saw what I would in any typical Scottsdale club, except maybe a notch or two cheaper decor, and with only a fraction (if even that) of the extremely hot female creatures that populate Scottsdale's clubs. This really aggravated me once I got inside, because of how hard it was to get in. Me and the group of friends I came with (which included some young attractive females) arrived at Level at 12:30 am on a Saturday night. There was no line. Nonetheless, the 3 bouncers hired to keep the riff-raff out (I saw not one soul other than us as we walked through the parking lot, for the record) told us we had to "wait in line" for a while. This was purportedly to make sure the maximum capacity of the club wasn't breached. This illusion created by the bouncers was unfortunately shattered when they, before our very eyes, allowed at least 10 douchebags in right in front of us. Why? Because they had "VIP" status. It took everything I had to keep myself from telling those goons, "It's 12:30. In TUCSON. This isn't Beverly Hills for f***'s sake." Finally, after an appropriate amount of time to convince us that Level is a very exclusive club where only sexy people are allowed and even then only after waiting for a long time, they invited us in. Insult was then added to injury when they demanded five dollars from each of us as a cover charge. As I said before, the interior was unremarkable and unimpressive given my expectations after the line fiasco. There was outdoor patio seating where many people were gathered, which is where I spent most of my time with friends. I of course enjoyed the company of my Tucsonan amigos. But the club itself is just a wretched, cheap, and unsuccessful imitation of Scottsdale. To top all of this off, I somehow reverted back to my irresponsible high school/college days as a Tucsonan and apparently forgot how to drink. Over the course of the evening I had 4 wines (pre-Level), two seven-and-sevens, 2 shots of rum and 1 shot of vodka. text: Araka makes a great first impression, with an absolutely stunning interior, replete with a comfortable crescent-shaped bar with an impressive two-story backbar and a sweeping design to the dining area that is at once open, but still affords a great deal of privacy, due to the way the tables are arranged. Off to the right, there are a number of cozy half-tables that are a perfect spot for a drink or two with a special someone. The other thing that immediately impresses about Araka is the service. From the hostess to the bartender, to the wait staff, Araka seems to pride itself on having some of the most friendly and attentive staff in St. Louis, or anywhere else for that matter. Meals are perfectly paced, drinks never get too empty, and the staff knows each dish inside and out and can make recommendations that you can trust. With such inspired design and service, it is a bit disappointing that the same cannot be said for the menu. Araka's food is very good, and in some cases excellent, but despite some nice presentation, there are surprisingly few standouts on the relatively small menu. Appetizers run a pretty standard path, with calamari and cheese plates, all of which are solid, but not spectacular. The salads are very fresh and all very good, but fairly standard. The one standout during the early courses is the watermelon gazpacho, which is probably the most unique offering on the menu. Not for everyone, but a very interesting mix of ingredients. The main courses are all solid, but with no real standouts. Most recently, I had the ravioli topped with lobster and peas. The ravioli was very solid, and the lobster meat was plentiful and fresh, but the peas and the pea-based puree that covered the dish were both very bland, and served as a black hole for flavor, making the entire thing just crash on the palate. Specials are offered that deviate from the path, but the regular menu, which consists of only 10 options, never seems to change. For a restaurant that puts so much into its image, it is perhaps a bit disappointing to see that the menu options don't rotate. The dessert selection suffers the same fate. Very limited, and very stagnant. The standout used to be the glazed donuts, but sometime in the past 6 months, they changed the donuts into donut holes, which lack the superior texture of the larger donuts. Why this change was made, I cannot fathom. All in all, Araka provides a great meal at a very reasonable price. First-time diners are sure to be impressed, and with good reason. However, the disappointingly limited and never-changing menu is a challenge to the repeat customer.

The place is filled with all sorts of delicious treats, and you'll have plenty of time to admire the cases and make your decision while you're waiting half of forever in line. Nothing good comes quickly, right? If you're going to get one thing, grab a canola. The shells are freshly baked, and they're hand filled to order. They're super delicious, not overly sweet either They do run out on occasion and when they're gone they're gone, so either order ahead of time or get there early if you're going on a weekend. The Sfogliatella is amazing with its mix of Ricotta and orange stuffed inside a flaky shell. Most people in line are pretty friendly, unless they're out of something. Then it seems people can get contentious over confections. It reminds me of the bakery I used to go to growing up in Maryland; owned by the same family across multiple generations, large curved glass cases, boxes wrapped up in string, and the best afternoon treats when you're out for a walk or place to pick up Sunday night dessert. Such simple treats made from well-practiced recipes honed to perfection over the years.
label: POS

The only down side about this place is that the owners/workers do not speak a lick of english so it can be hard to order and/or to figure out what you are really getting. The menu is partly in english. Regardless, I keep going back. Just gotta brush up on your spanish before you go.

text: Like Barbara C, we're usually fans of the sort of off-the-beaten-path rib shack, but the Smokey Bones in Brandon was a quick and easy choice on a rainy and hungry evening. The service we had there was top notch - so much so that we called the manager over to compliment our server. The ribs are decent, but the pulled pork is really the star. Great plain, even yummier with the mustard sauce. We liked the pulled pork so much that instead of dessert, we ordered a plate of pulled pork sliders. Our waitress noted that they'd been served to us without the pickle slices, and raced off to fix that. Normally my husband isn't a big fan of pickle slices (he's a pickle snob), but these were crisp and tasty and really did finish off the bread and meat perfectly. Don't order the roasted corn side dish, it's tasteless. Do order the broccoli if you have any fondness for broccoli at all. It's seasoned well, and we liked it so much we ordered an extra plate of it. The food alone was 3 or 4 stars, but the service bumps this place to 5.
label: POS

text: I dined at Fond with eight others the night before Thanksgiving. Service was excellent on all accounts, and it was clear that everyone on the staff was well-versed in all matters food and wine. The guys in our party opted for the tasting menu, while the ladies went for a regular three course meal. The tasting menu is typically only offered if the entire table participates, but we were accommodated due to the size of our group. I chose the mushroom risotto with hazelnuts and truffle to start. This was easily one of the best risottos in recent memory and I would highly recommend it. None of the ingredients overpowered and everything went very well together. My main course featured seared scallops, served with grilled romaine tossed in a Caesar aioli, with a roasted red pepper sauce alongside. Others at the table raved about this dish but I was a little underwhelmed myself. The fish special that one of the other girls ordered looked phenomenal, however. The men generously shared their dessert course with the fairer sex. A chocolate torte with crunchy hazelnuts was enjoyable, but the French press coffee I ordered stole the show. Passion fruit meringues were a dainty little treat that packed a flavorful punch to close out the meal. Fond's menu changes seasonally and there aren't many safe options for picky eaters, so leave those friends behind when planning a trip. I personally look forward to returning after the reincarnation of said menu!

We managed to find a dry table under an awning, which was nice--the rest of the place was a crush of people with nary a free table or chair in sight. Unfortunately, most of the beers our party tried to order simply weren't there; they were out, but hadn't been replaced yet. The beer that I DID try (Schuylkill punch, possibly?) was warm, flavorless, and simply unappealing. For the prices they were charging, having it served in plastic cups was just tacky. The food was unmemorable. Yep, I'm staying in the city from now on!

I had a veggie plate and highly recommend the sweet corn puddin' (served in a pastry shell) and the fried green tomatoes (best I've ever had). Prices were slightly higher than I expected based on location, but still very affordable. I was a tad underwhelmed by the $5 banana pudding so I'll try a different desert next time - and there will definitely be a next time. This would be a fabulous place to take family or out-of-towners.

text: After years of coming to Hipster Home, just to get drunk and covet nice things, I finally had reason to drop some dough there. My good friend Aaron was getting married. I hadn't been to a wedding in ages and wasn't sure about gift protocol. Gift card, registry, cold hard cash, what's a guy to do? Aaron and Lori are good enough friends that I didn't want to phone it in, I wanted it to be special. After deliberating over the matter for far too long, the idea of Hipster Home struck me. It was the perfect crime...get the Olks a great gift and give my business to a worthy store instead of Target. Dave and Lindsay were extremely helpful and generous with their time. Even though there were tons of great options for gifts, it was easy to find great wine and spirits accessories for the two lushes. Dave and I put together an amazing gift and Lindsay wrapped it up better than I ever could have. It was by far the prettiest gift at the ball ( so much so that when the card fell off, I was the last person they suspected as the giver). We waited impatiently for the feedback on our gift, and after a wonderful wedding and long European honeymoon, we finally got the news. It was a huge hit. Getting the gift at Hipster Home really made the difference. I recommend any person in the area, who is headin for a weddin , to eschew the gift card and registry route, and get yourself to Pheonixville. And if you are getting married in the near future, be sure to drop the HH name to your guests. You won't be disappointed.

text: Have to agree to Christopher to a point, those Gourmet Donuts are heavy. And there is a great coffee shop in the area that brews a better cup of the black stuff. BUT: This is mom and pop whipping up great baked goods. You don't get any "eat a dozen on the way home - light weight - Krispy Kreme" stuff here. One or two of these babies will hold you to lunch time. And this place is way cleaner than any Dunkin Dounut or most coffee shops I've ever seen. I got a peek at the prep area and, I swear, it could pass a white glove test. Note that the menu changes throughout the year. In the summer you will find something based on strawberries or some other fresh fruit. My favorite is the end of summer when the pumpkin spice donuts appear in the case. And they know the right way to make an apple fritter with big chunks of apple mixed into the batter (and not some apple sauce junk shot inside after baking) which is fried up with crispy edges and gobs of sugar. . . . Cherry Fritters . . . .don't even get me started. Or avoid the sugar with one of their fresh egg or meat pastries. I sometimes leave the house at the crack of dawn on Sunday to drive across town, pick up 5 dozen for various classroom request, and make it back across town in time for church. Toughest part is not eating two or three before I make the delivery. Say the word, "doughnut" to my smartphone and it dials Gourmet in Mt. Juiet.

text: After looking for an italian/pizza place to eat at in the middle of the day (many don't open for dinner until 5pm), I stumbled across this gem in my GPS. The service was very good- attentive and friendly although our waitress didn't introduce herself or the other waitress she was training. They kept my drink full and came around often to check on us. The booth seating was comfortable but the chairs/tables looked like they would be ok too. They do have a lounge area with a flat screen if you wanna grab some pizza and watch a game or something. Those tables are smaller and are high tops. I had a build your own pizza with mushrooms, bell peppers, and pepperoni. I was pleased to find that the mushrooms were fresh and large portobellos. The pizza had just the right amount of cheese and crust and there was an option to get whole wheat crust but we stuck with regular. My gf had the tomato, basil and mozzarella salad and it was really delicious. All the veggies were exceptionally fresh (the restaurant boasts that it buys local and organic). You can tell that they get fresh products. They even make their own mozzarella. We did have the bruschetta for an appetizer which was a bit disappointing- they were skimpy on the goat cheese and the bread was cut funny making it difficult to eat. We will probably go back and stick with sharing a pizza or salad and maybe try a panini. Each pizza is plenty for two people but probably not enough for three unless you aren't that hungry or get something in addition. They don't have many pasta options so keep that in mind when you go there. They have some unique desserts that looked good (including blueberry gelato) but I was too full to try them.
label: POS

text: This unassuming restaurant has really top notch Mediterranean food. The name is pretty generic, but the food is full of flavor and variety. The restaurant is located in the business park on Maryland Way in Brentwood so it does a good deal of business over the lunch hour. They have a full menu and a long list of lunch specials. The lunch specials include tasty dishes such as the veggie platter, which comes with very fresh tabouli salad, smooth creamy hummus, lightly fried falafel, and a large portion of lentil rice. All of this is only six bucks. It's refreshing to have such a flavorful vegetarian meal for so cheap. They also serve lamb, chicken, and beef gyros or platters with tabouli and hummus. The restaurant has a nice outdoor patio that is right next to a huge pond with geese and ducks walking along the shore. So you can get a little nature show while you have a bite to eat. Oh yeah, and they have a nice beer selection.

text: Brunchie Bruncherson is back with a review of brunch at The Scottish Arms. (This is not a dinner or bar review, so please note that up front.) And, maybe I should give it another try, but I do not have an endless supply of money, nor do most of us. It is usually a first impression/one try kind of thing with me. OK...so, I REALLY wanted to like this place as did my companions on our recent jaunt to this little Scottish haunt in Midtown/CWE. We are always looking for new and interesting places, and this spot had it all. Interesting decor. No huge crowds. A menu that looked super enticing and would hold our interest. Um...oops. Not so much. Let's start with the food. The menu contains some interesting items that are a-typical of an American brunch which makes things fun. (Like baked apples, oatmeal pancakes, bangers, etc.) Unfortunately, some of the items don't deliver, especially the basic ones. We all tried omelettes, and they seriously lacked some flavor. Eggs are bland on their own, so you need to add, at the very least, salt and pepper. Apparently, they didn't think this was necessary. Note to staff: it was and is. The potatoes served on the side were OK (if they were cooked). The sausage wrapped in rolls were nice. I ordered toast and marmalade, too. The marmalade was basically orange rinds with some gooey sauce. Um...no thanks. For drinks, the coffee was good: not too bitter. Juices were fine. I ordered a bloody mary and was given a glass of just ice and vodka. I had to go into the bar to finish my bloody mary. OK...that is fine with me since I could make it as spicy as I want. But I have about HAD IT with self-service brunch/restaurants! This ain't a work-a-raunt! Restaurant owners: ENOUGH OF THIS! Serve the coffee, make the drinks, make the food, serve the food. Basics. Urgh. So, the food wasn't all that spectacular especially for the price. But, the big downside was the kitchen. We were one of four tables in the dining room, and the bar had a few watching a soccer match. So, the place was not packed by any means. Yet, it took seemingly forever for our food to be delivered. And then, there was a major screw-up in our order. In short, the kitchen did not make two of our four omelettes. Yup, that's right: half the orders. So, two of us ate our bland omelettes while the other two watched us. I guess the kitchen didn't see this as a major problem because other tables were served, time went by, seasons changed, and it took another "forever" for the other two omelettes to come on out. Bad bad bad bad bad. (P.S. I have cooked eggs before. It does not take TEN MINUTES for two omelettes especially when you messed up the order in the first place. Notice Brunchie's internal temperate rising.) OK, so fine. The food came late. The waiter was super apologetic. I'm better. I know the food service industry is hard (especially when customers actually expect you to serve food), so I was willing to let it all pass. I knew what was coming, anyway. The owner or manager would stop by, apologize to the table, and comp one of the meals or both meals. Here they come. Just wait for it. They'll be here any minute now. I mean, of COURSE they will. They comped the friggin' bacon for the table next to ours when it was seconds late; SURELY they will comp some lousy eggs. But, oh no, they did not. Fail. Big time fail. No manager visit. No comp. We paid the full price. Done - two stars it is. Again, I am NOT one to berate restaurants or servers. It is a hard job. There is a lot to do, and customers are super demanding a-holes for the most part. I try to be the best eater out there and be as friendly as possible. But, this was too much. And, no, I will not ask to speak to the manager because that isn't my job. (Maybe there it is since I had to make my own drink.) Instead, I will pay my full bill, tip the waiter generously, and never, ever go back. And, that is where I stand on Scottish Arms. Two stars. Not returning. It really makes me sad, too, because, like I said, I really wanted to like this place.
label: NEG

text: Cannolis, cakes, cookies, cream puffs oh my... I have recently discovered my sweet tooth. It was always lurking in the shadows but for over 20 years I considered myself a salt over sweet kinda gal. However, I can no longer truthfully say that and Isgro's has for certain contributed to this change. To make matters worse, Isgro's provides quite possibly over 30 different varieties of baked goods. I have tried maybe half of those. The prices seem a bit steep at first but you can easily fill a box of cannolis and cakes and another box of mixed cookies for around $20. The cannolis are great, not the best I've ever had but I come from a town known for its cannoli so that's only fair. The cookies are awesome and for someone who could normally care less about a simple butter cookie, I would give my right arm for one of the butter cookies topped with sprinkles. The chocolate cakes are rich and wonderful. The cream puffs are standard good (although eat them right away because they don't fare well over time). And the raspberry thumbprint cookies are seriously out of this world. Writing this review is just making me want to head down to the Italian Market for another visit. If you're smart, I might see you there!

text: If you need tires, or you need to have a nail pulled out of your tire (like me) and you are in South County, have your car towed here. These guys are so nice and honest (shocking I know!). We brought the car in, they immediately put it up on the riser, blew it up, patched it, and we were on our way in 20 minutes. Best part, they only charged $20 for this, so much better than most of the schemey tire shops I have been in during my life. We also got a quote for new tires, and even that was reasonable. Granted, I am not getting new tires since I am not made of money, but it is nice to know where I stand before the winter time snow and ice festival begins in St. Louis. They weren't pushy about forcing us into buying the tires either, just gave us a quote and said to make an appointment when were ready. Unpushy mechanics?? Are they unicorns? Oh, and all the men that work here are incredibly good looking. So, maybe they are unicorns...

text: You'll pay buttloads for dinner and a movie here, but you'll most likely enjoy yourself. We came here to see Alice in Wonderland in 3D, and I had very few quibbles. And, brothers and sisters in Yelp, I pride myself on my quibbling. There are no shorter tables -- only stools at the bar and at a sort of dining-ledge in the lobby -- so wheelchair users dining in the lobby make do with a folding tray table. The staff was quick to assemble an impromptu dining area for the four of us, and cheerful about it as well. Cocktails are around $10 each, but made with good ingredients; I wish I'd sampled one but my wallet has no regrets. The dinner salad ($7) was a fair size, but not really enough for a dinner by itself. On the other hand, compare it to a $7 dinner salad at any diner-type restaurant and you'll be impressed (as I was) with the fig vinaigrette, grape tomatoes, broccoli rabe, chunks of fig, and mixed greens. Usually $7 just gets you iceberg, chicken tenders, and ranch dressing in a taco bowl. Pasta with vegetables ($12) was properly cooked, which you'll never catch me saying about comparably priced noodles at Olive Garden, and came with more broccoli rabe and yellow and red grape tomatoes. It would be easy to spend this kind of money at another theater and get food much worse in quality. You won't be writing home to Mother about the noodles and veggies, but they're better than most. The theater itself is top-notch, with roomy armchairs built with swiveling tables big enough for dinner and cupholders big enough for the gargantuan (and refillable) soda tumblers. You can even get a footrest if you ask. With luxury like this, I was mildly disappointed by the restrooms. I half-expected a machine to take a whiz for me, but -- and here's that quibble I promised you -- I had to urinate without mechanical assistance. There you have it: a sharply critical review of CineBistro Hyde Park. As Ferris Bueller might say: if you have the means, I highly recommend taking in dinner and a movie here.

text: I first took my daughter to Dr. Weaver last spring. He's an orthodontist but also a dental surgeon. I thought she might have to have that done (her teeth took almost two years to come in). After having been to various dentists all of whom couldn't tell us what was wrong with my daughter for over a year, Dr. JAW (his name is James A. Weaver) took ONE look at her and knew what it was. I seriously started crying. It was such a relief to hear that it was something that could be dealt with. She ended up having an excess portion of her gums removed and all the teeth were already there. Throughout the whole experience, Dr. JAW and his staff were amazing and kind. They understood that my daughter was little and scared and they did the best to make her comfortable. She has now continued to see him for early treatment and will eventually get braces there. I am very happy that she is in this early treatment because he can keep a constant tally on what teeth are coming in, which ones are still baby teeth, or if she needs any removed. When the time comes to get the braces, they'll tell us. Another great thing I love about Dr. JAW is that he has a Dr. JAW Smiles Club. In this club, the kids earn points in various contests. They are always sending out goodies in the mail which my daughter loves and really looks forward to. They send out newsletters, games, pencils, toothbrushes, puzzles, birthday cards, tooth boxes (for the tooth fairy) and lots of other things. The points the kids earn can be redeemed for various prizes including an iPod. I love all the attention they pay to keep the kids (and more importantly, the parents) happy. All I ever got in the mail from my dentist was a bill. I always recommend Dr. JAW to anyone who will listen. I am so happy that we found him and could not ask for a better dentist or a nicer staff.

text: PLEASE USE YOUR ROOM SAFE!!! I'm very torn about this review. The room was decent, the service was decent, and the price certainly represents a good value. The pool and gym were also really nice and I have no complaints at all about the above. But here is the incident that really puts a wet blanket on my review. I went there with a few of my friends to see a concert and, fish, and catch up. We went to the concert on a Saturday night and were out quite late. The next morning my friend noticed that there was a business card on his dresser that he must not have noticed the night before. The business card was from an escort! On the back of the card there was a note that read, "Thanks for getting me out in the rain for nothing. You should have canceled." We can only deduce that some "John" staying at the hotel gave her the wrong room number or she was in the wrong wing of the hotel. This must have happened while we were at the concert. Since my friend was staying in his room alone either a hotel employee let her in or the front desk clerk gave her a key. The hotel security is going to pull the hall surveillance tapes and do a key lock audit and let my friend know what happened. Bottom line is that the hotel let an escort into my friend's room while we were out. Luckily he had put his computer and cash into the room safe or I think he would have been robbed. I really enjoyed the stay at the the hotel and everything seemed good except for this incident, but this is a pretty big incident. I also have to say that the hotel security staff was cynical and even went so far as to ask my friend if he had visited any "Gentlemen's Clubs" that evening. It was pretty rude and we didn't care for his insinuations. I certainly hope that after the hotel concludes their investigation they have a good explanation and are forthcoming with an apology to my friend. In any case, I've learned an important lesson. Always use your room safe. PS - after the investigation is complete, I'll update this review.

I rarely crave red meat, so I had forgotten how scrumptious a great steak can be. The peppercorn cream sauce was divine, and the steak was so tender I could cut through it with my butter knife. text: I am definitely a fan of this place. I went to this tiny little shack on 8/21/08 with my family. My parents aren't usually a fan of non-Asian cuisine so it was a shocker when they wanted to try out the Shellfish Company. Points for luring in my very Asian parents. Even more points for not scaring them away with outrageous prices. Everything was reasonably priced, with oyster shooters being only $2.50 each. My bro tried one and loved it. If you look at the shooter, it looks like someone just tossed the ingredients for a pizza into a shot glass and stuck a raw oyster at the bottom. Hideously unappealing. I guess looks aren't everything, huh? You MUST try their steamed rock crabs. They charge by the pound ($6.50/lb), and they are fiiiiiiillled with delicious, juicy crab meat. Those babies were hard though, and we had to ask the waitress to take them back and smash them to pieces for us. The crabs came with marinara-horseradish sauce (soo good) and caramelly-butter (too buttery for me). Be sure to look out for their specials...I think for $24 you can get a 3LB crab, soup, and cole slaw. There were some specials on spider crabs too, but I didn't pay too much attention. One downside to this place is the wait...no, not for a seat, but for a waitress to come by. The service was really slow even though the place was nearly empty. We didn't even ask them to clean out the crabs for us so basically all they had to do was find us 3 crabs, toss them into the water, and serve them on a clean plate. One other thing, the crab shells were caked with sand. It put me off a little, but I will forgive them because the meal was pleasant. I originally was going to give SBSC 3.5 stars, but looking back on my experience I actually had a fun time sitting by the waters watching my parents suck the insides out of those cute chubby crabs. They were so round and cute that I almost had trouble eating mine. I wanted to keep it as a pet, even though it was obviously dead. 4 stars for you Santa Barbara Shellfish Company...4 stars!

text: I have had the privilege of working for one of the most premiere athletic clubs in the United States, Lakeshore Athletic Club, but have also attended the smallest, most mom and pop gym in a podunk town that had one stop light. SuperFit was referred to me by another client who attends the gym. I was instructed that it was a "no frills" kind of atmosphere and very bare bones as to what was offered in your monthly dues. She wasn't kidding. For starters, I do not understand how this place stays in business. They have two kinds of memberships: a basic which is $50 down and $10.99/mo or a $19.99/mo plan. The cheaper plan is bare bones, come and go as you please. The more expensive plan allows you to bring guests (unlimited) and also allows you to use their one tanning bed. They have no cap on the amount of times you can bring the same person, so they are getting a membership for free on your tab. And trust me, they don't check who is signing in everyday. They barely look up at you to see who is coming or going. The times I go in, there's no one sitting at the desk. The fact that they have tanning as an option has no merit on what I was looking for. If I was looking to get skin cancer, I'd prefer to be out in the sunshine. The staff: for the most part, when they are around, they are "there." I've gone to ask them about trainers or copies of my statements. 9 times out of 10, they have no information on the trainers they have in house (which, to be honest, are none -- they have a few that use the gym as their personal haven to train, but they aren't "Super Fit" trainers or employed by the company). I find this to be sketchy, because you have one trainer charging $40/session and another charging $65. Nothing is uniform and it gets a bit ridiculous trying to figure it all out. Most of the staff do not know how to use the computer system so don't ask them difficult questions. Equipment: the equipment is standard, at best. To the person who said the equipment is new -- that's a big, fat, N-O. All of their equipment is refurbished, meaning, yes, it was new at one time, but it's been overhauled with newer parts, but is old, or used and purchased from a place like "Play It Again Sports" or similiar warehouse. But no, the equipment isn't new. The treadmills (there are approximately 20) hardly ever work. I've had to jump treadmills mid-run because the one I'm on will automatically shut down with a failure error, which is a huge pain. You move to another one and THAT one is broken. None of the elliptical, cross trainer or stationary bikes are calibrated, which means, if you are on Level 1 or Level 10, it's the exact same resistance. This is how I know the machines are refurbished -- you need someone who knows how to maintain the machines to fix the calibration. Very disappointing. They also have weights and circuit training machines, however, it's hard to get into someone's rotation. People here aren't the most friendly and you may be waiting several minutes to use the machine you want. People are correct -- many of the users do NOT wipe down the machines and that grosses me out, especially when they are rubbing their heads or faces or adjusting themselves (men) and then go and use a machine to lift. They do provide spray and handtowels, but it's up to the the staff to enforce it. Also, you can never find a mat to do stretches. They only supply 4 or 5 for a gym that services over 300 users. The women's bathroom is always disgusting. I wouldn't use the showers if someone paid me to. They are gross - I went to use one and there was hair and remnents in the bottom that looked as though they had been there for more than a few weeks. There's rarely soap in the dispensers or towels. They do have parking, however, it is an unlined lot and most people do not seem to understand the concept of parking next to someone to allow space to get in or out of the vehicle OR park in a spot that could be enough for two cars. This is especially bad in winter when there's snow. Yes, they have tv's but there's no frequency posted that you can listen to the show/tv on your radio. The music they pipe in isn't what motivates me to exercise (Taylor Swift??) so I'd prefer to use my own form of music. Magazines don't make me want to join a gym so that holds no merit in my eyes either. The one plus is the hours. They have early/late hours on the weekends, which is beneficial to those who have to work. There is better out there, for sure. If Planet Fitness opens, they'll definitely have my business. Most likely, my membership here at SuperFit will conclude in the next month. I run and lift and circuit train -- all things that can be done with a jogging path, running shoes, and a few devices at home that I can get at WalMart. I'd rather save myself $132 and treat myself to a new wardrobe.

The list of potential positives is long and inspiring for those of us in the SOS (or is it Graduate Hospital, or is it Grey's Ferry, or is it SWCC...) Great location for the neighborhood, unique bi-level bar, flat screen tvs, adequate beer selection, jukebox, outdoor smoking area & edible bar food...so what's up? In a neighborhood desperate for watering holes, Yello Bar should be cleaning up! So why is it every time I go here, I find myself drinking in silence, whispering my orders to the bartender so as to not disturb the library style peace & quiet? Aside from the fact that I should probably find myself some friends, something is wrong with this picture. I almost feel like the joke's on me and all the real party people are setting the roof on fire in some secret downstairs celebration lair, laughing at all the nerds upstairs crying into our beers. I have my own hair. I have my own fingernails. I want to come to the party! Who do I need to know to gain access to the secret underworld of the Yello Bar? UPDATE: I've heard a rumor that Yello Bar has been bought by a new group...let's hope they kick it up a few hundred notches...

I was definitely surprised when what came out was a Japanese style curry. The mismatch of long grain rice and Japanese style curry was a bit disorienting for me. On the side of the rice and curry was a diced tomato-cucumber salad. After I tasted the curry, the first words that came to mind were bland, and I immediately began looking for hot sauce. Fortunately, a co-worker had done the same, as they wanted to spice up their stir-fry (though I think ordering a stir-fry at a pub is a mistake). In any case, the choices presented were Cholula, Tobascco, and I forget the third, but in any case, nothing that would be appropriate for a curry. I ate the bland curry, thinking that the curry powder must have been used primarily for color, and not flavor, and was dipping my fork into the chutney before every bite, trying to add some flavor. Unfortunately, the sweet mango chutney was practically a jam, and didn't do much for me. I could see a sweet chutney contrasting a spicy curry, but this curry was basically a yellow roux with some chicken and veggies, with no flavor. Anyway, two stars for being good for groups and accommodating, but no stars for the lackluster and disjointed dining experience.

text: I lived in one of the Robin Apartments for a couple of years just after moving to Philadelphia. Both the management team and the maintenance team are outstanding to work with and always responded to my issues both quickly and completely. When the freezer broke on my refrigerator they replaced the entire unit with a new one. When one of the motors on a ceiling fan died they replaced the entire unit with a new one. This may seem small, but having had to deal with half-dead appliances and shoddy fix-its with other apartments it meant a lot to know that this company didn't skimp on replacements to save a few dollars. The buildings themselves are in phenomenal locations; I believe they are all around Center City West. The only real downside I ever encountered was the pest issue. The buildings are extremely old and unless everyone in the building is mindful of the issue and takes action against it there really is only so much you can do. That being said, when I made sure to spray for bugs every month (set a little reminder on my calendar) I never saw a single bug for months at a time. My feeling on this though is that if you live in a city you kind of have to expect a little bit of an issue with pests. They are also really phenomenal about taking care of their tennants in simple and small ways. For one thing, the office will sign for and receive packages for you (and call to leave you a message letting you know they have it for you). Also, if you call them when the weather starts getting nice they will send a maintenance man to put your AC unit in the window for you. Not a huge deal, but for a single (at the time) 5'1'' woman with a 200 lb AC unit this became a seriously HUGE deal. I cannot say enough good things about the Robin family and the way they handle their business. It is also important that I mention that I have referred probably 10 different people to Robin Apartments. I know of at least four that have ended up renting and all of them could not be happier with the price and location. Tell me another place where you can find a one bedroom apartment with utilities included in Center City for under $650 and I'll point out that it is probably a Robin Apts building.

text: Overpriced and limited selection. Depending on your style this place may be perfect for you. I can honestly say that I didn't see a single thing that I couldn't live without. My boyfriend and I have a toddler, and because of that we needed to go from a queen size bed to a king. With a name like "Bed Bath and Beyond" I figured I'd find something I liked, for sure. The name makes it sound like it's a whole world of comforters... that and basically the whole back corner of the store is piled with bed sets. I should mention that the employees are always 'helpful' - almost annoyingly so. You walk in, and instantly someone is trying to 'help you'...then walk down the aisle to get to the back and every section you pass someone is offerring their assistance. Maybe some people like to shop like that, but I can't stand that. It feels like going to look at cars or furniture- they jump on you the second you walk near them and follow you around. Aaack. Back off, I'll find you if I need help! So yea, the whole back corner is filled with bed sets. UGLY bed sets that are ridiculously overpriced. And if you really look, the space they take up isn't indicative of a large selection- it's the same ugly sets- over and over again. Wal-mart had some of the exact same sets, for a third of the price. I'm looking around, and aisle after aisle it's the same bed sets in Queen and California King. So I ask one of the ladies who works there, where the King size stuff is- she informs me that BB&B is a "california king store". *Pause for reaction* Um, HUH? Wtf? You guys don't sell king size bed sets? No? WHY? She didn't have an answer for that- and she was looking at me like this was common knowledge and I was the only one that didn't know they don't sell king size items. Apparently the rest world either has tiny beds, or gigantic ones. No in between. A king size bed set is a 'special order'- yet they have a California King "Twilight" bed set. No joke. Obviously, I left empty handed. On average their bed sets are about $250. None of them, that I saw- had the sheets included either. So you'd be lookin at about another $80 at least- for a decent set of sheets. I personally think that's a little ridiculous- but I'd absolutely pay it if they had something I liked, in the right size. I ended up going to Burlington and found a gorgeous 10pc set (it came with a few of the throw pillows), a set of 600 thread count e.c. sheets, and two name brand king size pillows, all for around $115. My advice: unless you need six people helping you find a California King Size Twilight bed set, skip this place and go to Burlington or TJ Maxx.

text: When I go to a French restaurant, I am prepared for small portions, snooty service, straighten-your-back and whisper-when-you-talk kinda atmosphere. Then there's Miel.... I made reservations one day prior for 6 people, then 9, then 12 with Seema, the co-owner. She was very patient and accommodating. Although she could not get us in until 9:30, which was a little late, the night was perfect. The atmosphere is unpretentious and modernly-sheek. The dining room is small and sexy. There is no bar. There are no tourists. There are little locals. This is NOT a 'see-and-be-seen' type of place. This a place for intimacy (a rarity in Nashville). The wines are mostly California and French. We started with the foie gras & dates appetizer. The portion was at least 5 oz. (goodbye size 2). The fattiness of the foie was cut by the sweetness of the date. Delicious and melted in my mouth. My entree was the apple-encrusted salmon with bacon glace. Everything is better with pork - and salmon is (now) no exception. I love the French in Tennessee!! We stayed for 3 hours and never felt rushed. The Phillips have something very special here. Highly recommended.
label: POS

text: You remember that scene in Vacation where they drive through St. Louis (Well it's supposed to be ESL, but they screwed that up)? Roll em up. But man, Old St Louis is like Beirut, except with Church's, it was hard to believer the area was just a few miles from my place. (Sorry wanted to make people aware). Suddenly you see a nice block and nice cars, is this heaven, not it's Crown. Man, I imagine my grandfather coming in here as a kid and it looking the same, I think I saw Wally and the Beav sipping on a malt. Seriously though, this place has the best BLT and Malt I've ever had (although, I don't know what the difference between a shake and malt is , just add malt?). The bacon for the blt is kettle cooked, I'm not exactly sure what that means, but I liked kettle cooked chips, so I assume it's some type of frying. The BLT is as good as they come. The malts, there are so many to pick, but I would suggest sharing it, don't try and be a hero, very rich, so keep up with the water as well. text: This is the single best place in Philadelphia. I could leave it at that but I'll go a little deeper. If you are visiting Philly, you have to include Reading Terminal Market. Best to go Wednesday through Saturday when the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants are open. The market is open Sundays but a number of merchants are closed. You might think it is a tourist trap. It is to a degree. However, most of the people there are locals. Tourists can't sustain the meat, fish and produce shops that are there. So no shame, none, ever associated with it. Its not like being a New Yorker and going to Times Square for a meal. The market is closed at 6PM, which is one of the few drawbacks: it has no evening hours. I hope one day that will somehow change. Also, it can be overwhelming. Lunch rush is intense and finding a seat to enjoy that roast pork sandwich can be a challenge. I went there during lunch rush of the week between Christmas and New Year's and I have never seen it that crazy. So that's not the best time to go because hundreds of suburbanites like myself get the same idea to enjoy Reading Terminal with their day off. For breakfast the options are limited. There is the Down Home Diner which is decent but I'm not kvelling about it. Some of the stands do breakfast but I haven't really tried them. I finally tried Profi's Creperie and it is pretty good. My suggestions about food if you're there one time during a Philly visit: If it is Wednesday-Saturday, go to the Hatville Farms deli counter and get a smoked turkey special with iced-tea and potato chips. Hatville Farms is one of the Pennsylvania Dutch merchants and I swear that the smoked turkey special is the best thing in all of Reading Terminal Market. Plus, they have stools at their counter so you don't have to go looking for a seat. If it is Sunday-Tuesday, go to DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef. The line will be long but it moves fairly quick. Get the roast pork Italiano with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone. That's a Philly sandwich! Reading Terminal Market, you are what makes New Yorkers jealous of Philadelphia!

text: Looking for something to do this Halloween, and can't bare another lame haunted house, and the 2 hour wait to get into said lameness? Have I got the solution for you. Every year the Historic Indpls neighborhood of Irvington becomes Halloween Town, with everything from a Beauty Pageant to a Gothic Cabaret to satisfy your lust for spookiness. Check out their website for a full program of events, but I'll go a head and give you a few of the highlights here. Irvington ghost walking tours, buy Irvington ghost tours soup & sprits curiosity shop, every Fri & Sat night in Oct. Tour starts at 7pm and leads off from 6 S. Johnson Ave. For $15 dollars you get not only a guided tour of a beautiful old neighborhood, & all the ghostly dirt to go along with that, but also a book with all the story's found there in. That's good value for your entertainment $, One tip wear very comfy shoes, when they say it's a walking tour, they really mean hike. Cabaret Poe. An original musical piece based on the works of Edgar Allan Poe. Wonderfully Gothic musical housed at Irvingtons Haunted Masonic Lodge #666 (I kid you not the 666 is etched in limestone on the front of the building for all to see) Halloween Costume parade, the highlight of the festival, they shut down Washington St. so the kids (big & small) can march right down the middle of it in full costumed glee. Parade always held the Sat. before Halloween. If you don't have a great neighborhood to take the kids trick or treating in I recommend this one. Included in the Festival is a House decorating contest for the entire neighborhood. So you get to check out all the decorations as you "beg for candy" door to door in a picturesque setting with a blanket of leaves from century old trees lining the twisting streets to carpet your every step. Festival runs last full week before Halloween. 2010 festival dates: Oct. 23rd - Oct. 30th.

text: I took a minute to read some reviews. Bored with that, I decided to write my own. The food here is average at best. I had the grilled chicken in lemon pepper something marinade. That, in of itself, was decent. The steamed broccoli lacked any crispness whatsoever. It had the consistency of cooked pasta. Not al dente. Pasta you started cooking, then you wake up from an unintended nap 30 minutes later with most of the water slurped up into your noodles. You could cut through the broc with your finger and chew it with gingivitis gums, sans teeth. We noticed there's no refills on fountain drinks. This is a solid money maker given the summertime weather. I'm shocked they don't sell tube socks full of baby powder to keep your undercarriage from rashing up, at a premium of course. The salad was a standard, no frills lettuce mix with too few tomatoes. I like tomatoes so the aforementioned lack thereof is always disappointing to me. My life is cluttered with hardship. This brings me to dessert. Which is a sport at Remoulade. Go ahead, try the brownie a la mode. Do yourself a favor and go a la mode only. The brownie was near impossible to cut with a fork--imagine play doh several years old that has been sitting outside the container. Coated in epoxy. You could play ice hockey with it. Needless to say, it was gross. Made the folks at the table wonder if they were laughing while using a dremel to cut the slices for us. The jumbalaya looked good, the meat pie, not so much. Oh, and the bread that came out as an appetite-wetting nibbler, no taste, and not robust enough to put butter on. Kind of like cotton candy, but notnearly as tasty. Remolaude is OK if your taste buds aren't mature...for me, not worth the no-wait to be seated.

text: A few months ago I had an incident at this Superfresh. They had a promotion going on and all the signage was very confusing, so I spoke with a customer service person to get a better understanding. I then spent an hour shopping and making very specific selections with the purpose of buying items that would maximize taking advantage of this promotion. But when I got to the checkout, it turned out that it had been explained to me all wrong. I was being given about 1/100th of what I had expected to receive out of this promotion. I asked to speak to a manager, and got bumped up and up and up to different people, all of them telling me there was nothing they could do. Ultimately I left behind my entire basket of groceries. I found everyone to be rude and, frankly, to not have a store honor the word of an employee is not only unfair, it's against the law. (Google "Implied Authority of Contract".) I ended up going VERY high up in the SuperFresh chain of command, talking to someone in their legal department who deals with their contests and promotions. I was ultimately mailed a package with what I was denied at the store (even though I didn't even buy the items.) I told this person that I would take a break from this store location and try again later. So after waiting half a year, I went back to this store yesterday. I shopped for 20 minutes. Because of a public transportation strike, the place was packed, and I waited in line for about 20 minutes. Then, while there were still 3 people in front of me, the checkout man pointed to the woman in front of me and said "Miss, you will be my last customer." I was flabbergasted. Trying to maintain my cool, I said "Excuse me? I was already in this line for 20 minutes! You can't just make me move to another line." The man, clearly NOT sorry or concerned with me, said "That's just how it is." "No, that's not acceptable," I replied. "We all understand that sometimes you have to close your line down, but you do so by telling NEWLY ARRIVED people that the line has been closed down. You don't make someone who was already waiting in the line move to another line with 15 people in it." Though I was not yelling or raising my voice, it became one of those situations where the people in line around me were rolling their eyes at me. That's kind of a shame, because I wonder how they would feel if they were in my situation. "Could you please point out the manager to me?" I said to the checkout person, who at this point would neither speak to me or make eye contact with me. So I wheeled myself over to customer service - a familiar area - and asked to speak to a manager. I explained the situation, and I also explained that I was abandoning the $100 in groceries I had intended to buy, and that this time, I was not ever coming back.

text: As my stomach starts its predictable pre-lunch growling, I can't stop thinking about the delicious meal I had last night at My Thai. My date and I were under the impression that the place was a BYO, but we were quickly informed that there was indeed a liquor license. We made our bottle of brew disappear and ordered some Sapporos instead. I'm almost positive that's Japanese for Coors Light. No matter; a light beer went just fine with the spicy flavors of our main courses. For me, that included a heaping plate of chicken and shrimp with baby corn, onions, peppers and cashews in a mildly spicy brown sauce (him-ma-pan shrimp and chicken). White rice was served on the side, as well as some steamed veggies which included broccoli, carrots and cabbage. The extra veggies were a nice touch and a welcome alternative to the rice, which my boyfriend gladly accepted. His pot of chicken and veggies in a lemongrass scented broth was far hotter and more complex in flavor. While I am personally not a big fan of lemongrass, he enjoyed the dish and said he would order it again. I was more than pleased with my choice, which I polished off without much help. The cost of dinner was in line with and probably even less than many of the gastropubs we frequent. After our lovely meal, we agreed to make more of an effort to step outside the box when choosing a weeknight dining destination.

text: Located outside the technical limits of Tucson, their standard labor rate is a good 4 dollars less than in the city. Couple that with my pity story and my student status, and I got another 4 dollars off labor ($44 is standard). After having my car totaled by an uninsured driver and receiving a less than adequate payout from my insurance company, I needed a place that would fix my car with parts that I brought it, not new parts that they ordered, and make my car look new again. I checked reviews and the better business bureau, and decided that this place would do a good job of re-making my car. Ina Road Auto Collision, or Spectrum Auto Paint and Collision, I can't figure out which name they go by, was a horrible experience. Customer service is just awful and the work they do does not appear to be top notch. The experience started off well. Because my car was rendered immobile, they came to my house to write up an estimate. They did require a large window of time on a Friday morning/afternoon, but the man who came was friendly. I did some preliminary work on my car and drove it to the shop. When I dropped off the car I had them write a new estimate substituting the parts I brought in. I explicitly told the man writing this up that I wanted a scratch on my trunk lid to be fixed and that I wanted all dents to be filled in on the used parts I was bringing in. I was quoted 1 week. One week later I received a phone call that my car was ready for pick up. They offer door-to-door service, but could not pick me up because 10 miles is too far for them to come and get me. So I paid a cab 30 dollars to drop me off at the shop. I sat down and was asked how I would like to pay. "I'd like to see my car before I pay." I sat at the receptionist's desk for ten minutes before being told that my car was not ready. I insisted that someone drive me home. Two hours later I was driven home. A week after this I got a second phone call that my car was ready. I insisted again that they pick me up, and they did, and as we pulled into the parking lot I could see my finished car. At least this time I knew it was done. I walked around the car and saw that none of the dents were filled in and they did not fix the scratch on the trunk lid like I asked. I talked to the man who wrote the second estimate, and he lied to me about what I told him during the initial estimate. I can't fathom a body shop that would just paint over dents. They also needed to pull out one of my fender aprons. After doing this, the bumper didn't fit right. There's an inch or so of space under the left headlights and millimeters under the right headlights. Pre-accident there was no space beneath either. I came expecting the same level of quality as at my California body shop and that was not what I got. Considering the other reviews of this place, people in Arizona must just have lower expectations.

I called the manager at Wagsworth and asked what happened and how it was overlooked. She said my dog was seen by the vet that morning and was fine. She suggested it may have happened when she saw me and got excited. I don't think you break a front tooth from that. But if their vet had actually opened her mouth, they would have noticed the mangled teeth. The manager gave me the run around and said next time they could have her in a plexiglass run. If they noticed her chewing on the bars why not move her then? I was told she was moved somewhere but not sure where. I am not happy at all with this kennel and am glad the agility classes I signed up for were canceled. I am also not happy with my $750 vet bill after her two night stay here. text: The IMA's collection rests on its chief benefactors, namely the Clowes, Lilly, Marmon and Pantzer families and their differing collecting tastes. While Indianapolis is a relatively old Midwestern city, the IMA's history is recent; it was known as the "Art Association" until 1969. The recent multi-year renovation, redevelopment and expansion of the Museum and grounds created an entirely new experience for art patrons. Let's all say our condolences to the Krannert Pavilion's Brutalist architecture of the 1970s and hello to a somewhat uninspired series of camera-ready atria that will no doubt allow some very impressive parties. The collection itself is conservative and unprovoking. Highlights include Robert Indiana's iconic masterwork (and trademark-infringed) "LOVE" painting and sculpture, a beautifully painted though incredibly ill-placed Rembrandt, a decent Hopper, an encyclopedic Asian art collection that is one of the best in the country, and the largest collection of JMW Turner drawings outside of Great Britain (although quantity does not trump quality). I thought the gift shop was as poorly stocked as the previous one. Not a single postcard of the new museum's exterior, yet there were plenty of old postcards showing the now-demolished Krannert Pavilion. And for an artwork that's been copied, dubiously appropriated and downright stolen, why was there not one postcard available of Robert Indiana's outdoor "LOVE" sculpture? And what about museum merchandise based off its own artwork: scarves with motif from the museum's Tiffany piece, jewelry pieces mimicking something from the Asian galleries or pop-up note cards laser-cut with the new museum facade? Sure, all the "LOVE" stuff is nice, but capitalize on other museum strengths. This is a wonderful museum that has a decent collection. The parking is free, the new eating options are terrific, and there are other fun attractions on the museum grounds, most notably the Lilly estate, Oldfields.
label: POS

text: That's funny: John W. drives to San Francisco to see indie and foreign films that will never come to your local multiplex, and I hop on a plane and find myself munching popcorn (with REAL BUTTER) and enjoying a couple of outstanding movies here. For us film-lovers, I guess the grass is always greener ... especially, as John says, if you happen to live in Phoenix. I knew I liked Tucson better, and The Loft is one more reason why. The main theater is a classic big-screen theater from the 60s or 70s. I have yet to see anything in the smaller screening rooms. For some reason, I had thought this was like the Arlington Cinema N Drafthouse in Virginia, which has several local beers on draft and a kitchen. So I was a little disappointed to discover what looked like a conventional concession counter. They do have a couple of beers and ciders on tap, and a selection of bottled brews, but the pizza is by-the-slice from under a hot lamp. It wasn't bad, but still. The pleasant surprises included the popcorn (did I say REAL BUTTER?) and how friendly the staff were. I was very pleased to be able to see some great films, including one from China that I know won't be generally distributed. The Loft is a membership organization; supported by people who love the art of cinema. If I were here more often, I'd definitely join. If YOU live here, and you love the cinema, you should consider playing a supporting role at one of the best cultural institutions in your town.

I try not to hate on anything "free," but when your free comped dessert takes forever to arrive and is BURNT, what is one to do? Two out of three weren't bad, but they weren't good either.

text: Extra star for the staff and volunteers who were SO friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. They really seemed like they enjoyed what they were doing and enjoyed talking to the visitors. You didn't have to ask them much, they would offer information just as you needed it. They really knew their stuff. There isn't a whole lot here, so don't expect Sea World or the Long Beach Aquarium, but there is enough to entertain you for an hour and a half or so. And if you are going to be strolling along Stearn's wharf, why not stop in and pet a shark, hold a star fish, or let some hermit crabs crawl in the palm of your hand. It's about 8 bucks for adults and it all goes to a worthy cause. Highlights: Petting the little sharks, holding the crabs and starfish, the actual shark eggs with living embryos inside (they are weird!! It has a lot of interactive stuff to do, mainly geared for kids. But we adults enjoyed ourselves and even bought trinkets for the well stocked gift shop. I find it hard to beleive this is not reviewed yet. If its posted someone where else, let me know.

Whatever. Arriving at Sabrina's it seemed like the multiple hostesses were totally overwhelmed. While waiting for a table, I was concerned that, in the chaos, my table would be given to a party that arrived after me. As it turned out, the wait was a bit stressful but not very long at all. I may have lucked out. The fact that I only needed a table for two might have also helped. Point being, don't let the long lines scare you away but be prepared to wait. The wait was well worth it. We ordered the special pumpkin pancakes and an omelet. Both items were amazing. Some of the best brunch food I've ever had. The food was well prepared and really tasty. Even the coffee was top-notch. As some of reviewers have noted, the crowd on the weekend can be a bit obnoxious. If you are allergic to hipsters, it might be worth avoiding the weekend scene. Also, a long wait in the cold could be bothersome as there isn't much standing room inside. Still, even after tolerating the hipsters and long waits, Sabrina's is definitely worth a visit.
