text: Sophia's reminds me of my favorite Greek diner in Chicago. Well, 'cept it's not open 24 hrs. Best way to describe Sophia's is like a marriage of LePeep and the Original House of Pancakes. Interior is bright n sunny, well-lit space. Open 7 days a week closes at 3pm. Huge menu. Like, compete-with-Cheesecake-Factory-it's-practically-that-big-menu. Egg eggs eggs, paninis, all varieties of waffles/pancakes/french toast/crepes, sandwiches, burgers, soup, salads, you get the point. First thing you're asked when you sit down is, regular or decaf? It's okay coffee. It's strong enough. It's better than McDs. It's the southside. I go for their most excellent egg white omelets (or regular omelets) bc i love breakfast food and would eat breakfast for dinner every other day if my boyfriend let me. They have over 10 house ones around $7 or you could create-your-own too, w/ none of that crazy $2-per-extra ingred nonsense a la Patachou et al (don't get me wrong, I'm a huge longtime fan of Patachou too. but you know, places are different). Off the top of my head that includes Denver, Western, Spartan, Michigan (cheddar n apple), Hawaiian, they even have an artichoke-mozarella-parmesan one. Anyway, the only thing that would take it to a perfect-10 is if they served em in the skillet, also w/ a "Pam" option, instead of butter. Comes with hashbrowns & your choice of toast or 2 pancakes (well actually they have this long list of possible side options too, but do people actually eat cottage cheese with their omelets?), yeah it's a LOT of food. I always switch out the potatoes for fresh fruit-- usually banana, canteloupe, orange, pineapple. Really nice. If you do stick with the hash browns, they're done right, come w/ a perfectly browned crust. Moist n fluffy pancakes, as much hot syrup as you need. If you are going for lunch, traditional club sandwich is my rec, get the fries, they are really good fries!! they will make them however you like-- if you like em limp n blonde, you get limp n blonde. Me, I require structure-- golden-brown and crunchy. they've delivered product every time. (Likewise, they will customize your omelet for you too-- easy on the cheese, heavy on the veggies, etc.) Friends have also enjoyed the country fried steak, corned beef hash, BLT. Huge fresh salads.... well all-in-all huge portions if it hasn't been made apparent yet! good value. Friendly & competent service, those ladies work for and deserve their tips. oh-- if you like to judge places by the quality of the jams on the table- they serve Dickenson's. that's good jam. that's not cutting corners.

text: The only logical explanation for the lack of rhyme-or-reason to the layout of this open-air mall is that it must have been constructed in stages not planned in advance. Part of its perimeter is lined with a meandering of stores; in its center are two islands, one anchored by Michael's, the other by Target, each with a cluster of shops adjacent to it; and a few chain restaurants and a bank are scattered about, like little boats lost at sea. Separating these areas are parking lots so vast that it's impossible to leave your car in one spot and walk from one section to another. How user-friendly is a mall that requires you to park several times if you want to cover all of it? Most oddly-located is a multiplex theater, tightly tucked in a corner that has the fewest parking spots of all. You'll find quite a few independently-owned businesses, which normally I like to support, but too little variety in what they're offering . . . two pet shops, half a dozen shoe stores, and numerous clothing outlets provide too much competition among themselves and more than enough confusion for shoppers. This is a place to go only with a specific destination in mind . . . browsers should go elsewhere, especially on a rainy day.

text: The service was a little slow, and they don't have a ton of space, but I have two words for you: Turkish Burps. My boyfriend and I were in Turkey last year, and everywhere we went there was a complimentary Turkish breakfast. The same exact thing everything time: Bread with butter and homemade jam or preserves, olives, slices of cucumbers, plum tomatoes, a few cheeses, and a hardboiled egg. I know, weird, right? Well, we ate it every morning for two weeks and it was always a great way to start the day. We kept saying we'd buy all the stuff to have a Turkish breakfast at home, but it's such an odd assortment of foods that we never got around to it.... They we found out about Cafe Fulya! We split a Turkish breakfast platter, I got my strong Turkish tea and he got a Turkish coffee and we walked down memory lane. It was perfect. The bread was what did it, I think. I don't know what it is that makes the bread Turkish, but it tasted just like Turkey. The country. The kicker, though, is that after we sat there for a while, digesting, I burped. And the burp tasted like the breakfast all rolled into one and I got one of those wonderful sense memories and it truly made my day. I'm so glad that there is a place in Philadelphia that can give me Turkish Burps! I half wish that this place was on my way to work, because I would get tea every day. However, it's saving me lots of money to have this place in the opposite direction of my route to work. Lastly, the baklava: Very good. I don't know if it's the best I've ever had. I can't think of any, specifically, that's been better, but it didn't knock my socks off like I expected. It's very, very good, though.

Four stars for being a bit more complex with cuisine than necessary (in my opinion) and for the somewhat high prices. But after all, this is NJ and you get what you pay for. text: I think I may have scared our server at Zinburger. Not that a table of six highly boisterous people walking in toward the tail end of the night on July 4th wouldn't be intimidating... I think it was more so my pointed questions about how food was prepared, whom the executive chef was, whether the restaurant was in a restaurant group, and if they had a beer sommelier that really threw him off. Zinburger has this very contemporary look, with lots of exposed metal moldings, simple clean lines, a very open dining room, and a number of wall-mounted flat panel TVs. As the name would indicate, it's a mash-up between a wine bar and an upscale burger joint, with most burgers rolling around the $10 range. Not much for a DCer to bat an eyelash at (hello, Central, I'm talking about you) but definitely not cheap by Tucsonian standards. Between the lot of us, we ended up trying many different burgers, and the boy got the seared ahi salad (beautiful and tasty - I'm glad they brought the dressing on the side... it would have been a bit much poured on it). My Samburger was done up just medium - great and juicy beef patty with a slice of cheese melted on top. Although the menu mentions that it's served with Thousand Island, I didn't really notice. What got my attention was the savory smoky bacon on top. Mmm! The only garnish with the burger were three slices of pickles (which I nibbled on in between bites of meaty joy). Even before I bit into my burger, I was already a little tipsy from my draft Sierra Nevada - they have a number of great microbrews on tap! Who does wine with burger? Not that I disapprove - I just find it much more satisfying with a cold one. And apparently so did everyone else in my party. Plus, our fries came out as quasi-appetizers. Sweet potato chips were meh. The yogurt sauce was good, but they need to be a little thicker so you can actually taste any sweet potato. Double truffle fries were typical truffles frites with truffle aioli. Surprising for Tucson, but not as good as Poste's in DC. Zucchini fries were the winner for me - cover in parmesan, these little nibbles were a mite crispy, but very tender when you bit into them. The Ranch dressing became dangerous the more I imbibed. Don't forget to check out the interestingly decorated restrooms before ditching out of Zinburger. Ladies - ever wanted to know what it feels like to be hounded by the paparazzi? Wonder no longer, just go and take a whiz!

text: Note: This review is for their lunch buffet. I normally don't give 5 stars on a first visit, but every now and then I have one of those transcendental experiences where I reach a state of pure bliss. The lunch buffet at Everest on Sunday afternoon was one of those times. We woke up a bit rattled from the revelry of the previous night. Our brains were still tender, our bodies craved warm caloric sustinence. I checked Yelp and some blessed soul had just posted a review for Everest. I made sure that the lunch buffet was available on Sunday, and we were off. Arrived at 1pm, greeted by calming Eastern music and a "Namaste" from our host. Aaahhh. We are seated at the last available table in the intimate little dining room, other diners murmuring softly around us. The outdoor sunlight illuminates the space just right. The buffet sits in its own little room in the back. We walk in and immediately are enveloped in lovely Indian food aromas. There are 3 types of chicken, lots of veggie dishes, rice, naan, sweets, and more. Everything is just great. The tandoori naan has that light char to it. The chicken is tender and tasty. The clear Korean noodles are great and full of flavor. The vegetable korma has broccoli, which is not often used in Indian cooking, but is cooked just right. Nothing is too heavy or greasy, as Everest puts a lot of importance on healthy eating. Everything is just perfect. My body says 'thank you'. We end on a sweet note with the mango pudding. WOW. What an ideal way to cap off our amazing meal. A rich smooth texture, just the right amount of sweetness and bursting with the essence of mango. I briefly wonder if it can be administered through an IV. We don't want to leave this place, but people are waiting for our table, so we pay the check ($10 per person) and walk out with full bellies, goofy smiles, and a deep sense of gratitude to live in these modern times.

text: Visited New Orleans for the New Year.... This was about the only good thing about the hotel. New Year's eve we slept in and missed the available cleaning times. No big deal, we had gotten in late. New Years day the cleaners came and made the bed, that was it. We were shocked, they left our dirty glasses, didn't take the dirty towels despite leaving them on the ground as instructed when we wanted them changed. Much to my horror the cleaners rehung a washcloth that was clearly soiled. They emptied the garbage, but left our champagne buckets and empty bottle. They did NOTHING else. We are not messy people and do not require much in the way of cleaning, but we do have expectations when it comes to hotels. As it turned out this was the only time our room was serviced during our 5 day stay. In particular I spoke with the man at the front desk and let him know that we would be stepping out for half the day and would like our room serviced...by then it was day 3. He said of course, when we returned five hours later, the room had not been cleaned. I was furious at this point. Again the next day the room was not serviced because we were in the room at the time that was convenient for the hotel staff. Unbelievable. When I tried to talk with the front desk staff about it, all I got was excuses. Not apologies, not "how can we make this better?", nothing. In fact they made it seem as though it was our fault for being in our room in the middle of the afternoon or early morning. When we checked out I was so disgusted with our room I was beside myself. The front desk again failed to acknowledge fault on their part and offered us no compensation. Additionally I think I may have gotten food poisoning from room service, which came without trays and in plastic containers and cost over $150, which I didn't realize until the next day! We had a terrible cheese plate, a soup, salad, and some fish. $150? Really? So so so disappointed. I will never go back. Don't order the food and don't stay if you like a clean room.

The hostess on the phone told me that there might be a "little" wait, but not more than 15-20min. Fine. Jump ahead to 8:45p - we arrive early, expecting to go up to the lounge for some drinks while we waited for our reservation. 9:15p comes, and we ask about our seats - we're told that it will be a little longer. Fine. Jump ahead to 10:00p - we ask a waitress to check on our table, as it's now been 45 min. since our reservation - she never comes back. We then ask a different server the same question - she comes back about 15 min. later to tell us that our seats still aren't available. At this point, one would think that the server/hostess would have the sense to at least offer us peanuts and the option maybe to sit at an actual table, if the sushi bar is over-crowded. Of the three hostesses hovering around the hostess stand, their combined brain cells could not come up with any alternative options or consolation items. We saw people in the lounge, who were seated well after us, being led to their tables/seats before us. After paying our $78 check (for 4 drinks) and being told several times that we would have to wait "a little longer," we finally decided to leave. The food is good at Morimoto, but there's no restaurant where the food is worth waiting over one hour, especially when you have a reservation. It was like a Seinfeld episode - what's the point of a reservation?! Word to the wise - if you want good sushi, there are better places than Morimoto; if you want good martinis/drinks, there are better places than Morimoto; if you want omakase, it's worth trying once at Morimoto, but you are a sucker if you get it again & again - the whole point of omakase is that the menu should be created on the day of w/ the freshest ingredients specific to that day - Morimoto's omakase is a cookie-cutter menu with slight variations (i.e.: maybe they give you hamachi instead of toro). On our way out, my friend complained one of the vapid, brainless hostesses, who did nothing but say "I'm sorry." Yes, you should be sorry - you just lost 3 customers!

text: In short, I felt like it was the Disney World version of what great jazz should be/used to be in New Orleans. Kind of steep, but worth paying for a good show. Then, a few benches in a big room with rickety ceiling fans and not dim enough lighting. I wanted a real low, sultry, steamy place with old guys smoking at the bar and women in day dresses parked at their usual seat, foot tapping in rhythm. Instead I got tourists upon tourists (yeah, I was one too) and a few high as a kite stoners seated on the floor. It wasn't a good start, and I made the comment to my dad before the band started up their 3rd set that I felt like we were about to be the butt of some horrible prank by NOLA residents against obnoxious tourists. Then the band started to play. Some of them were incredibly talented: even my untrained ear could tell there was a good amount of skill there. They were taking requests from the crowd, and as a result ended up playing a bunch of ragtime "hits" instead of the more typical "jam" sessions I had expected. Plus, after each song, they hit you up for money. Yes, I know NOLA is still hurting and I'm sure you've got kids to feed, but after the $10 cover the whole thing just felt like a complete and total sell out. I'd skip Preservation Hall, despite it's grand history. I think Duke's rolling in his grave over this one.

text: Though I don't get there as often as I would like due to the location, I love Mama's House! There used to be another Korean restaurant in Fishers, but now I think Mama's House and Bando are the only two left?? At any rate, I've never tried Bando because Mama's is such a sure thing. The restaurant is easy to miss thanks to its very unassuming location in a strip mall that has seen better days. The last time I was there, the parking lot had more potholes than not....but that may no longer be the case :-) However, don't let the outside scare you away - Mama's has fab Korean food. The first time I went I was immediately transported back to a college friend's dinner table. She was Korean and I knew I'd found some good eats when I recognized several items at Mama's that my friend used to cook for her dinner parties. I've had both the traditional Bulgogi dinner and the Bibimbap. It is hard to say which I prefer. The bulgogi is nice if you have a larger group and the experience of Bulgogi is definitely unique...you cook your own meat over a charcoal brazier built in to the table and then assemble Korean-style "tacos" with lettuce leaves, rice and bits of the Panchan - Korean side dishes that are like relishes and pickles (the best!!!) - and some sauce. The Bibimbap is like Korea's answer to a noodle bowl. In this version, you'll get a bowl of rice topped with a variety of delicious and perfectly prepared vegetables, some sliced meat and perhaps an egg (optional at Mama's House), plus just enough chili paste to make things meld together ideally. Serious comfort food in a single bowl! Like the Bulgogi dinner, Bibimbap at Mama's House comes with a number of Panchan (side dishes). These little morsels are probably what I love most about Korean cuisine....little bites of Kimchee, marinated mushrooms, beansprouts, cucumbers....you get the idea. The panchan are also replenished as needed at no extra charge, so if your party finds something they really like, you won't run out during the course of your meal! If you haven't tried Korean food and you are an Asian foodie, you must make haste to Mama's House :-) PS: everything here goes down extra well with a Korean beer.

text: My boyfriend took me here recently for my birthday dinner, and it was truly a wonderful experience. After going there, I can definitely understand how popular it is regardless of what time of the day. The interior is wonderful - dark wood floors and furniture highlighted with creamy linens. It can feel a bit crowded when its full, but not uncomfortably so. The kitchen is also partially open to the dining area, with a bar right there (ideal eating location in my opinion), and the bar itself is on the side, partitioned off from diners. The food is delicious; it was very hard to choose only a few, especially since they offer so many traditional spanish tapas. The full entrees seem unnecessary compared to the tapas since we weren't even interested in them. We had: Escalivada: Roasted Peppers & Eggplant, Cippolini Onions & Confit Tomatoes (really good, but would skip next time) Morels Salteados: Morel Mushrooms, Thyme & White Asparagus (exquisite - its small, but very memorable) Grilled Baby Squid (simple but cooked to perfection, they were amazingly tender) Arroz de Langosta: Lobster Bomba Rice with Clams, Lemon Zest & Golden Pea Shoots (MmmMmm gooooood) Pimientos de Padron: Fried Peppers, Sea Salt & Salbitxada (delicately spicy - a must) Piquillos Rellenos: Crab-Stuffed Peppers (If you get one dish, this is the one. Amazingly good) Olas de Chocolate: Godiva Liqueur Cake, Chocolate Mousse, Milk Chocolate Ice Cream (definitely for the chocolate lover, and surprisingly large compared to the tapas) Banana Torrijas: Crispy Spanish Bread, Carmelized Bananas, Maple Syrup Ice Cream, Banana Anglaise (TO. DIE. FOR. If you like bananas, that is) We also each had a glass of sangria; I had the tinto, which was incredible and lived up to the ones I've had in Spain, while my boyfriend had their seasonal bianco with mint and mango, which he loved but was too sweet for my taste (weird, because I'm the one with the sweet tooth). The portions are smaller than some might expect, especially with some dishes, but for the two of us those 6 plates, two desserts, and sangria was perfect - however, it does leave a substantial bill at the end of the evening. However, we both agreed (especially me since I didn't pay ;D ) that it was completely worth it. And the service was spectacular, we had a very attentive, informed waiter. This is truly one of Philly's top restaurants.

They have 10 taps: 3 were local craft beers, 2 were other crafts, 3 were popular Belgian imports (Hoegaarden, Lindeman's Framboise and Stella, yuck) and 2 were popular Irish imports (Guiness and Smithwick's). They had one craft beer on special for $4 all night. We thought the food was quite good. The Shepherd's pie was tasty, though came with no sides and cost around $12. My girlfriends, whom is a vegetarian, really enjoyed her veggie sandwich with roasted veggies and feta cheese. My other friend got a pulled pork sandwich that looked great with tasty fries. We've previously had much drunken fun in the small downstairs (basement) bar. So, we'll go with 4 stars.

They tightened the belt for me, free of charge, and filled me in on the rest of my car's issues (it's an ancient 94 mercury villagers with 200k+ miles). There was no hard or soft sell. He just told me what he thought the best course of action was for me (which didn't involve me paying him for anything more). text: Dim Sum Garden is a good place everyone should try once. The place is called Dim Sum Garden so one may think you should come here and eat dim dum, but the place doesn't serve dim sum. Don't worry though there is something much better on the menu. At Dim Sum Garden, they serve Shanghainese soup dumpings, called xiao long bao. Its the first and second item on the menu. If you don't know what Shanghainese dumplings are, let me explain to you. These aren't your regular dumplings. Each dumping is a little pouch filled with meat but also this rich gelatinous soup. When the dumplings are made, an icecube of stock is also wrapped in there with the meat forming a soup dumpling when it is later steamed. When you eat these dumplings don't just pop them in your mouth. They are piping hot! And don't bite into it spilling the juices all over your shirt and plate. If you do, you just wasted the best part. Instead grab one out, put it on the spoon, bite off a little piece of the skin and slurp the soup out of the dumpling. A little vinegar soy sauce may be added to the dumpling too. Then consume the whole dumpling. Repeat 7 more times, since each basket comes with 8 dumplings. Go to Dim Sum Garden and order the Shanghainese dumplings. There are other items on the menu but I don't think I will ever get around to eating them, except for the scallion pancakes. To my knowledge this is the only place in philly you can get Shanghainese dumplings. If you are familiar with Joe's Shanghai in NYC, this philly equivalent is just as good. I think they're damn good eats and at 5 bucks a basket you can get a great snack anytime of the day.

text: OK, this is certainly not the best sushi I have ever had, but it is consistently good. Actually, I think it is really good, especially for the price. I think every time I have been here I have gotten their Las Vegas Roll. It is just that good. Their caterpillar roll is also delicious. Nigiri style cuts are nicely done as well. I just tried the red surf clam for the first time and it was delicious. The yellowtail on my last visit was also very good. One thing I really like about Sushi Garden over other places is that they don't use nearly as much rice for the rolls. I'm wanting my rolls concentrating on the fish, not the rice, when I go out for sushi. Many places in Tucson don't seem to get that. Another great thing about this place is that they still have the $19.95 all-you-can-eat option. I wish there was tiered pricing though, where a second person could get the same thing for say, $14.95, but that is likely just me being greedy. They also have an all-you-can-eat buffet for lunch, which appears to take place on Saturdays as well now. The choices for sushi from the buffet are indeed limited to a couple types of rolls (no sashimi or nigiri), but there are also many standards from a Chinese-style menu. It's honestly not my thing as I'd rather get the sushi I want, but judging by the crowds here at lunchtime, it is certainly a hit. And really, it is great to have the option. Seating at Sushi Garden can seem a little tight at times, when crowded, but still there is generally seating available immediately, and it is accommodating for a couple as well as for larger parties. The sushi bar is one of the longer ones I've seen in Tucson, and perfect for a "bachelor's" night out as you can sit at the bar, chow sushi, chat with one of the chefs, and watch a game (typically baseball or soccer is on one of the many TVs viewable from the bar). I used to do this here constantly years ago when I lived right down the street. Overall, there's some tweaking that I would personally like to see happen here, but that still doesn't change the fact that this is a nice place to get sushi, with many options that you just aren't going to find at other sushi joints in town. Someday, I'll get to the one by Foothills Mall and see how they compare.

text: Yay for my 200th review, and a 5-star one to boot! We came here with our group of 10, Groupon in tow ($75 for 10 people, 2 hours of bowling, shoe rental, and 6 appetizers). They didn't treat us like crap just because we had already paid. In fact, service was VERY attentive and we had someone coming by every 20 minutes or so to make sure we had everything we needed. We had the following appetizers, and I think we all appreciated the fact that they waited for all of us to arrive-- food came out hot and fresh, not cold and rubbery because it was out too early. 1) crab and cheese dip 2) mac and cheese bites 3) loaded potato skins 4) buffalo chicken bites 5) artichoke and spinach dip 6) cheeseburger sliders I was able to try everything except the artichoke and spinach dip and the cheeseburger sliders. Very very good, although the buffalo chicken bites were a tad on the dry side. The loaded potato skins are to die for! You seriously do not get food this good at bowling alleys...I'm so used to buying a grease bomb at an overpriced stand. This was a pleasant surprise. I was particularly impressed by the look of the bowling alley. We pulled up, parked, and said something along the lines of "Oh man, I wonder if this is one of those old-fashioned bowling alleys." NOPE! It was absolutely gorgeous inside (did they renovate recently?). The shoes were brand new, or so they seemed, because they were still stiff and clean. The balls weren't all chipped and grimy, plus they had a good selection of weights and finger sizes. Bathrooms are spotless. Our entire group had so much fun and some friendly competition. Thank you, Pinsetter!

text: Go here. It's different than anything else you'll do while in NOLA and very educational. And as a super-duper added bonus, the food is damn good. I finally got a glimpse of what gumbo was supposed to taste like after being severely underwhelmed at K-Paul's the night before. Great for both small and large groups, adults, children, teens, foodies, non-foodies, and even vegetarians (he'll make you a salad). You'll learn about the history of the city via the history of the cuisine in a fun, casual, air-conditioned environment. What more could you ask for for $27? And lest you think that all the Yelpers giving it 5 stars are friends of the place, check out other review sites (blasephemous, I know, but Yelp has yet to reach critical mass in NOLA). text: A bright and tidy shop with a wonderfully diverse range of mature flavors that slightly balances the bubblegum pink interior. I walked in dead set on getting the honey fig macarpone gelato, but then I saw the pink grapefruit and had to try it. As luck would have it, samples are happily doled out. The pink grapefruit was delicious, really delicious. The small size serving is $4. I have no idea how much the other sizes are, I don't even recall seeing a price list. You just have to walk in with the mindset that prices be damned, you want gelato and you will have it. And if you get the medium or large size, you can get a combination of flavors. For the immediate downtown neighborhood, alternatives are mainstream ice cream or fro-yo. So really, there aren't suitable alternatives. But, I cannot give them the top rating in good faith because the gelato is brought in from out of town. And greater Santa Barbara does have another gelato shop that does produce locally. In the end I stuck to my guns and got the honey fig mascarpone. I will be back for the pink grapefruit, I promise. Final note: the girls that work there unfortunately have to dress like hoochies. It slightly cheapened the experience for me, but it might please others.

text: I was searching for a hairstylist and a friend recommended this place. I'm accustomed to paying a fair amount to get my haircut - I see an expensive haircut as a much better investment than an expensive shirt - but my bill here came to $80 including tip! This was for a 10-minute cut to recreate the long layers that my old stylist had done 6 months previous. No drastic change - I liked the cut I already had, I just needed to get rid of the split ends. I should also mention that I arrived 5 minutes early for my 3:30 appointment, and was kept waiting until 4:00, without even an apology when the stylist finally came out to get me. I was OK with the cut I received, but I had LOVED the cut from my old stylist, and that one only cost me $56 (and that price includes a 50% tip). I think it will be worth my while to drive the 500+ miles to my old stylist. One plus though - the environment was very relaxing, and I enjoyed the experience until I saw the bill and the final result.
label: NEG

text: In my book this is the best nightclub in the city if you love latin music. I prefer to go on Saturdays. The crowd is less tense and everybody is looking for a good time. Dj Safarii is the resident DJ and is a fantastic, fantastic DJ. He mixes bachata, merengue, salsa and some good house and trance music. There is a giant dance floor in the middle which can fit over 1,000 people. The lighting in the club is great and there are two bars on the outsides of the dance floor. It is never too crowded nor impossible to get a drink. Drinks are reasonably priced. The place tends to stay open past 2 normally between 2:30-3am. While it is in a bad neighborhood there is constant security around the club/restaurant, the crowd on Saturday night are older late 20s-early 30s all looking to dance and have a good time. The perfect place to end your night if you're looking to dance! All of the normal tendencies you see at nightclubs do not apply here. You don't have to worry about the braggadocios machismo guy looking to pick fights and look tough; The bartenders who are more interested in finding the drunkest chick in the club/bar than serving you drinks and the overpriced everything that comes along with the clubbing experience. It is good drinks, great music, a relaxed crowd and great atmosphere.
label: POS

text: On nights where I had to get work done, or felt anti-social and didn't want to hang out with anyone, or got in the night before everyone else and had no one with whom to be social, I would order from Tazza, a recommendation from the hotel staff. When you look at the menu, you realize there's a lot going on. It's hard to choose when you have about five pages of choices to choose from. It's a case of a small business trying to cater to too many tastes. It's even more overwhelming when you factor in dessert, which I never got to. The first time I ordered from them, I had it delivered to my room. Waiting for 45 minutes for food when you're hungry now is a bit of a downer, but they were nice enough to give me my drink for free. I ordered a "small" stromboli and a pasta, which barely fit in the mini-fridge in my room when I had leftovers. The 'boli was good, but the sauce in the pasta was a little bland. The second time I ordered, I went to pick it up, hoping to cut down on the wait time (20 minutes). Again, I ordered the pasta, hoping that the first time was a fluke, along with a cheeseburger and fries, which I'm told is their specialty. The burger was massive and good, but the fries were a little soggy. And sadly, the pasta sauce was still bland. The prices were okay, only because of the sheer volume of food involved. Still, I'd be okay paying the same amount for less but better tasting food.
label: NEG

text: i love love love django. Get the gnocchi, whatever kind they offer that night, they are sickly good. had an amazing scallop dish with braised pork, chorizo and potato puree. it was sublime. the homemade bread is so f-ing good. cheese plate is great. desserts aren't my favorite there. only one problem was i wanted to wrap my leftovers but the waitress accidentally threw it out. they made me a whole new meal to take home. so nice. would go back again and again.

text: how i ended up at the only bar in philly without a beer week event is beyond me... oh well, we went. i have to say, i looove belgian beers so was really happy when my friend suggested we check this place out tonight. i was also intrigued by the menu. i've never eaten fondue so i don't have much to compare it to but i felt underwhelmed by my cheesy pot and pile of bread and sausage. the bread was chewy (is it supposed to be for fondue)? my friend had the meatball app -- he felt they were too salty. i had a cup of soup too. we spent more than i would think for 4 beers, a fondue plate and 2 apps. hum, maybe just stick to beers here next time?

text: Here's another reason to cope with hunger: Nevada buffet places! Not so healthy, but enough to pick and choose your calorie intake for dinner. An average of two plates and you can send yourself into food coma and feeling guilty in the morning just by looking at the mirror. What the hell did I eat last night?! The only highlights: Prime Rib (get the medium rare portions). Don't settle for the dry portions. Build your taco or nachos. Steamed shrimp & crab legs Desserts (take the fresh baked cookies and get a scoop of vanilla ice cream - make an It's It out of it!). Skip everything else! You'll know what I mean even before making your selection. Venue: Remind me of an oversized Rainforest Caf. Don't worry...you're not hallucinating! If you had a lot to drink ( or your medication kicking in ) Yes..the trees do move. Price: $26.99 per person on Saturday and Sundays. If you're staying at the Peppermill, you can use the $5.00 off coupon. Great for large groups: Yes. Large dining area for family and friends. Keep in mind that this place gets busy for dinner so reservations are recommended in advance. One extra service for our friendly and attentive waitress: Even though you're serving yourself at the buffet, the wait staff works their butts off to remove your used dishes and refill on drinks. Please tip generously. One this night, we dropped $25.00 for our waitress. Thank you!
label: NEG

text: The service was friendly and attentive. The food was a solid 3.5. The music was fabulous. I had the shrimp creole and the gumbo soup. If they are authentic, they both require a "stomach", and here they were a good try but not strong and stewy enough. The location is also fantastic. Don't make it your choice if it's the only place you can go to, but for a good bite with a nice ambiance, it's a sure thing.
label: POS

text: I used to adore Delachaise back when I lived nearer to Uptown. it definitely had the potential to be one of my more favored bars in New Orleans, but I haven't been there lately. Anyway, to put it succinctly this is more like a junior wine bar than a fully stock OMG WINE!!! bar. It does also offer a nice array of beers for you manly men out there who refuse to touch wine (look, I know you exist!). There's also a nice selection of appetizers or full on meals to accompany your various adult beverages. I've only had some of the sampler platter, vegan options are sparse, but my friends who've ordered the other items have all been quite pleased. The venue itself is an elongated shape - shotgun style, perhaps? There are tables, seats, bar stools etc. kind of just shoved wherever they would fit - very limited is what I'm trying to say. As per usual, a very dimly lit establishment - possibly a nice date destination as it's usually not incredibly rowdy in here. I very much like Delachaise because it feels like it's a happening bar, without it being actually ramped up and happenin' - if you know what I mean. It's been the location of many nice evenings with friends - just chatting away, drinking wine, and chillaxing. This isn't the cheapest place, can be a little moderately pricey, but you pay for the ambiance and food and alcohol selection, I suppose.
label: POS

text: Filthy. The food at this place has gotten worse and worse as the years go by. I used to love this chain, now it is on my s#%t list. Which makes me sad. The tacos I had were just gross, salty, old meat with old onions and cilantro. My husband though I was lying so he tried it and spit it out (he will eat anything so this is a bad sign). The beans had some nasty smelling cheese on em and it really turned me off. The worst part of the whole experience is the dirtyness of the eating area: sticky food laden floors, wet and food covered tables, unkempt drinks area. The managers/owners of these places should be ashamed and hopefully will get the message before its too late.

text: I am changing my original review to this one, and never to return again, unless I am dying, no, unless a family member is dying. I myself, would rather die. The cashier in the pharmacy department was touching her eyes, face, and mouth without any apparent attempt to wash, rinse, or sanitize. This person is passing out someones medicine! We go there to get well, not to get sicker! This deplorable, unsanitary service will NOT be tolerated! Please at least do it behind something, so we physically can not see what it is you are doing. This is New Orleans, not Haiti! Not only are you infecting me, you are infecting the gentleman ahead of me, and the woman in front of him. AND the person who was behind me! DISGUSTING pharmacy clerks. So very disgusting. This is why I will try and give exact change and not take a receipt from you, so I do not have to touch whatever was coming out of your nose, running out of your eyes, dripping out of your mouth. Horrible, dirty clerk. I have already contacted corporate, but they aren't the ones spreading the germs. The locals need to know what is happening here. And also, when you cough, please do so in your shoulder or elbow, not your hand, as you are reaching for a item, change, or a thank you bag.

text: I've heard about Naked Pizza for a while, always with salivating taste buds and awe at the mere idea of what I was hearing. Then I tried it. and then I thought, "really?" I tasted no difference. I don't know what else to say. I was heart broken. Regeneli's is much higher on my list of good pizza.

text: I hope this place burns to the ground. Literally. My first summer in law school I figured I'd take a waitressing job here, after waitressing in SF and making a small fortune doing so. not only is the minimum wage with waitressing in nola $2 (vs. $9 something/hr in SF plus tips obviously, but i digress), but this place is run by incompetents. I'd always heard the food here sucked ass, but never tried it myself, and it was nearby, so in my random application process, i ended up here. The co-owner (wife) seemed nice, and when the barely literate 'manager' called me to come in to 'go over the menu' a couple nights later i was excited to begin working...I came in and they were shocked that i hadnt come in that am (apparently the imbecile who told me to come in that afternoon to 'look over the menu' meant to tell me to come in in the MORNING to TRAIN. as in not look over the freaking menu, but to actually begin working. either way, wouldnt typical protocol be to call me that morning when i didnt show?? having put this event in my phone, and being a responsible law school student, it seems fairly obvious to me that the 'management' is inept.). a couple days later, i was terminated for my failure to come in that am, to which i responded with a lengthly letter to the owner, that it was their managers fault, as she told me to come in that 'afternoon to look over the menu.' As i'm responsible, i brought waitress style clothing just to be safe, although i dont believe that would be implied when told to 'come in to look over the menu'. As i'm rambling now with rage 1.5 yrs later at the absolute idiocy that this place embodies, i'll discuss other details of the restaurant. As my friends had previously said, the food here is awful. bland bland bland. my boyfriend liked the margaritas as theyre fairly cheap, and we all repeatedly would get heartburn from the shitty jose. to top it all off, i have heard (and experienced nothing else myself), that the service is BEYOND poor. the staff is comprised of artsy assholes, who dont give a flying rats ass if you have any food/water/have ordered/have died at the table from food poisoning. literally, you will bus your own table and if you ever see a refill of water or anything else you are beyond lucky. everyone i know in nola has had nothing but negative experiences here, and after the first termination of my LIFE, due to someone elses incompetence, i have refused (as have all my friends) to ever set foot in this shit establishment again. if you like wasting money on bland food and god awful service then feel free, as the 'owner' informed me in response to my letter addressing my inappropriate termination, they were 'overhauling' the management. Strangely years later, i have still yet to hear anything good about nacho mamas.
label: NEG

text: Had dinner there twice over a few weeks ago, the second time was take-out. We came back because the food was really good - freshly made with quality ingredients and cooked to perfection. Pasta dishes are very good, the salads are exceptional. For the modest price, it is a very good value. p.s. check out the wine and cheese place next door while your order is being made.....

text: So me and my girlfriend had a 3 days 2 nights trip to Reno this weekend. After having dinner there for the first night, we decided to go back there for the second night dinner rather than trying the steakhouse in Silver legacy hotel. We ordered a plate of SPAGHETTI MARINARA and MEAT RAVIOLI, oh boy, that was delicious, and each plate costs only $12 each. The old gentlemen who served us gave me the best service I have ever had. Second day, we ordered the CHEF'S SURPRISE for $32 each, it is a four course meal that you don't know what the chef will cook for you. It was just okay, did not really impressed me. This is a really awesome restaurant to try. Food is great, service is the best, and the cost is just right. I wouldn't recommend ordering the chef's surprise if you are not really into Italian cuisine.

text: My wife and I decided on an early dinner and selected this OG. Still being somewhat new, they have some areas needing help. This was a "Sodium Chloride" banquet!!! Bread sticks are long rolls dusted with garlic salt. Mussels di Napoli sauce was salt laden butter in a lemonade type broth, Eggplant Parmigiana had to much breading and the pasta sauce employed salty catsup, Chicken Marsala was a huge serving(2.5, quarter inch chicken breasts with a salty-marsala sweet sauce. Our Minestrone and Fagioli soups were not distinctive enough in flavors. And yes, my Fagioli was quite salty. ( it is possible the chef/cooks work for a heart doctor who wants salt laden patients for treatments) The atmosphere/ambiance is good. Host/Hostess greeting-seating excellent. Waitress was basically OK, just kept over selling everything and was frequently apologizing for taking so much time getting something she forgot- like an entree- Also said she'd be right back so many times I thought I could get in a short nap in between her trips. We had a $50.00 gift card and dinner for two, no alcohol, 2 ice teas, 1 appetizer and bread sticks came to $47.78. I do believe the salt was free----- On a Foodie Note, I wouldn't call Olive Garden, Macaroni Grill, Buca De Bepe De Something, true Italian restaurants- Perhaps, a restaurant with an Italian Atmosphere, or Italian Flair might be more apropos. We'll try some other spots first.
label: NEG

But it's square pizza and they do the cheese under the sauce which it's pretty much amazing! I like the classic plain with mushrooms but we just branched out and ordered the veggie white pizza and it was awesome...will definitely be my new favorite!

text: Liquor stores are a dime a dozen in New Orleans, but the centrality of this one in the quarter and it's nice atmosphere always seem to draw me back. It's a very convenient store because most of the time I just want to get a drink and walk around without being really tied to any bar or anything. Getting drinks from bars in the quarter can get really expensive. Here, you can find all the normal things you could want at a good price. Go for the things on SALE. $3 bottles of Blue Nun, why not! Me and my girl each picked up these huge bottles of Blue Moon's limited edition "Grand Cru," each one being like 25 or so ounces and 8.5% alcohol for $5.00 each (down from $9.00 because the sell-by-date was coming up). $5 on that bottle was enough to get me drunk and make her throw up in the marriott later on in the evening. So, thank you very much. This store is nice haven from the ritual expensiveness of the rest of the quarter and I'll definitely be stopping in whenever I'm around to try to find out what's on sale.

text: All I can say about this place....AMAZINGLY fantastic and delicious. It TOTALLY lived up to every expectation I had from the appetizers, through the entree, then dessert. Even the wine list. The service was so on point and friendly...they were great. The gumbo was delicious and well-seasoned. The duck was mouth-wateringly good (is that a word?), and I don't even normally like duck. Everything was phenomenal, and as I've said before, I'm very critical. And honestly, the food was decently priced for the quality we got.

text: When you're just "over it" -- don't worry, there's a pub for that. For the most part, the Lockerbie stays true to its dive bar roots. Nothing fancy -- darts and pool, plenty of room to eat decent food, quench your thirst with plenty of beer choices (including some Sun Kings), and hang out with a low key crowd who are also probably hoping to evade most of the idiots, tourists, and yuppies you likely passed along the way to the bar. It didn't take them terribly long to know my usual order. Also, Jeff is one of the best bartenders and servers in the city, and he means business. Take my word for it until you discover for yourself.

text: Am I missing something? Are the burger joints around DC and Northern Virginia so ungodly awful that this chain makes the f&%#$ Zagat Guide for something like seven years in a row? I mean, the burgers are okay. I'm definitely not a fan of well-done, which is the only way your burger gets prepared (Boo. This is Americuh, dammit. I should git a choice!) I like the free toppings, but that's not really a special concept. And the fries are like the fries at Penn Station or the Philly steak place at the mall. Good, but again, not special. From the various signs with glowing reviews assaulting you from the moment you walk in, I just expected more. I guess I should have saved that eighth of a tank of gas and walked over to Crusoe's Original. Sigh.

text: I found this place by accident as it isn't very noticible tucked away in the strip mall, frontlined by the dingy little Robin Hood restaurant. We were going to go there first for lunch, but the menu looked overpriced and I expected it would just be the average diner food. Osaka Sushi looked nice and clean and decorated beautifully and the smell of delicious food made me decide to stay. The prices were awesome. My friend and I had the lunch special, $12 for all you can eat sushi rolls and one entree from the list. (You have to finish what you order though, or you will get charged for what you leave behind). My friend's shrimp tempura was awesome. I had the hibachi shrimp, which was a wonderful grilled flavor with a variety of veggies like zucchini and carrots. I think I'll get the tempura next time though because it was SO GOOD. We got an order of pork fried rice for the kids. Now let me ask you something... When was the last time you took a bite of pork fried rice, said mmmmm and your eyes rolled back into your head??? Yeah, never happened to me before either. Well, this time it did and I had a hard time not eating the kids' food!!! That was the best fried rice I've had in my life. FOR SERIOUS. Now to the sushi...I had the Alaska Roll (Salmon and avacado) and the fish was so fresh and both ingredients were of a generous size. Usually they skimp on something at most places. The spicy tuna roll was alright, but I think I should have gotten my favorite, the Unagi (eel/avacado) roll. It actually comes with cucumber but I prefer avacado. Anyway, I was going to make that my 3rd roll, but I was too full to order it haha. All I have to say is....I will DEFINITELY go back and even the kids liked the place. There aren't a lot of tables though, at least not big ones. This is a good place for a nice date, the atmosphere is classy and crisp, but the biggest table was a 6 seater in the center of the room, which is where we sat. I imagine if you wanted to take a large group, I would call in advance and have them move the tables together. There are no booths. They also have a take out menu with decent prices.
label: POS

text: OK ... the pizza wasn't as bad as it is in the cafeteria at work, but that's about all I can say about it. The service was slow and misguided. Our waiter was a nice guy, but not a very good waiter. He never cleared anything from the table, and when he realized he hadn't put any ice in our water glasses, he brought a glass of ice to the table and dumped it into our Pellegrino. He disappeared for long periods of time. And, when he brought back the check after running my credit card, he forgot to bring a pen. And disappeared again. The food was not very good. The focaccia brought to the table was damp and spongy. Our fried calamari appetizer was limp and greasy. The "roasted chicken" pizza was covered with dry, flavorless lumps of barely warmed chicken breast. The other ingredients had little flavor, apart from the occasional bursts of overdone garlic. We also had the Mr. C pizza, which was ... better than the other pizza. In order to bring some flavor to the meal, we asked for some grated cheese and red pepper flakes. We got the pepper flakes, and the waiter brought a cheese grater to the table, and offered to grate some cheese over our pizzas. We preferred to control the amount ourselves, and asked for a small bowl of grated cheese. He went away, and returned with a small bowl, but said his manager told him we would have to pay $1 for it. It wasn't worth it. The cheese was mild and next to flavorless, not the sharp, tasty parmesan we had been expecting. We did, however, get to "enjoy" a performance of "Volare" by the strolling accordionist. And let's not forget the almost unrecognizable synthesizer version of "New York, New York."
label: NEG

text: Stay away from Savannah's Cafe! We went to Savannah's for lunch today. The hostess made my coworker and I wait 8-10 minutes for no apparent reason, when there were open tables everywhere. When she finally seated us (at a table with no one nearby), we waited another five minutes or so, but no waiter/waitress. Then we saw two restaurant patrons who had just entered and they got seated immediately, and a waiter went to them. Was a secret handshake required to dine here? It sure felt that way. The worst customer service I've experienced at a restaurant. Will never go there again.

text: This has to have been the worst meal that I ever ate in my whole life. Started out with a truffle and potato soup which tastes like: wet cardboard. My main was a duck schnitzle which tasted like: dry cardboard. I was terribly, terribly disappointed in my meal there. I will never go back.
label: NEG

text: Garces is a rockstar. He is probably food god. And I don't even eat meat - but I'm pretty sure that if I did, he's be my personal hero. I'd want to be him when I grow up. THIS place is GENIUS. The concept of having a state store INSIDE a BYOB is amazing. Sheer genius. The wines were supposedly selected by Garces himself, and they were all relatively fairly priced. I like that they have a rotating special depending on the day of the week. The cheeses are great, I especially liked the accompaniments. The bread and olive oil was delicious. Me and my friend both ordered a pasta - I ordered the equivalent of spaghetti and meatballs minus the meatballs - but the pasta and sauce was some of the best I've ever had. I wish I could bottle it and eat it every day. We also tried the desert - and went with a plate of cookies. The rest of the dessert looked great, but was WAY too much for two people. I will go back when I have to go to a dinner party and my job is to bring dessert. I can't wait to go back. There are SO many things I still haven't tried. This is going to be my new place to visit regularly. Move over Tria!
label: POS

text: Food is average among the chinatown places but the service is extraordinarily bad even for chinese restaurants. Got takeout here once and had to wait over an hour, pestered the waiters a few times but they didn't even bother checking on the order, just said kitchen is busy. Probably would avoid in the future if I could.
label: NEG

text: 4.5 stars... Good Dog bar is one of my favorite bars in Philly. They have some great interesting beers both on tap and bottles (most are $5-6) but not so much as to let kegs go for weeks without being swapped out or to be overwhelmed by too many choices. At the same time they still have $3 bottles of cheaper light beers like Miller Light which keeps me happy. The bartenders have always been super friendly and their food is way beyond any typical bar food (try the pulled pork), it's downright awesome. The first floor is an intimate bar and a number of large comfortable booths, the second floor has a tiny bar and is mostly just tables and chairs (the first floor can fill up quickly during bust times), and the third floor has all the fun stuff. A dart board, pool table, pac-man, and one of those electronic gaming machines. One of the things I like a lot about the bar is that the walls are covered (artfully with frames) with b&w candid dog photos, it's really cute but not corny at all. If you like bars, and of course you do, you'll love Good Dog.
label: POS

text: I gave you 2 stars because I'm sure you do something positive, however, blocking the circluar drive at the Edward Jones Dome for an hour or more after the football game is not one of those things. Per the Dome employees who wheeled my in-laws down, the police (YES, YOU!) are supposed to let handicapped rides pass through to pick up their riders, not let the old people sit and rot for hours on end. text: Food was good as always (except for the pumpkin ravioli, three people at our table ordered it and none liked it). Service left much to be desired, our waitress was angry that we wanted to order appetizers. I think she had better things to do. Overall I think sabrinas is caught up in it's own hype and has let itself go.

text: Holy crap! What the heck is this place doing in the middle of Lansdowne? So, it took me forever to get here, through red light after red light on a Tuesday night, but when I got here it was outta sight! OK fine, I've had a few glasses of wine. Oh geez I rhymed again without trying. Must -- stop -- now. A friend and I had the Tuesday Tasting Menu, $49, 4 courses, and it was delightful! Scallops on a Jerusalem artichoke puree with bacon, brussels sprouts and a black truffle jus, absolutely perfectly executed, the scallop was done just right, not over or undercooked. Then the cheese plate, kinda nice, but not the highlight of the meal. Then on to the main course, pheasant 2 ways. A breast and a confit leg, and both were cooked to perfection, served on a celery root puree, and kale, and a prune sauce. The breast had stuffing, and in it were chestnuts. OH MY GOSH, it ain't Per Se or El Bulli, but it was absolutely BEAUTIFUL! Then dessert, 3 ways, a toffee thing, a tiramisu with BOOZE in it, oh my GOSH, MOST RESTAURANTS ARE AFRAID OF PUTTING BOOZE IN DESSERTS! Not here! Not a lot of booze though, just enough to add a little zing, not the kind of boozed-up dessert that only tastes of booze and nothing else, but just perfect. The third was a coffee ice cream, so you got the toffee/coffee thing goin' on throughout, and yeah, it was integrated and complimentary and just gorgeous. The staff was very friendly, and attentive, I will be coming back to this place real soon, and EVERYONE should also! If you don't get lost on the way....
label: POS

text: Their pizza and wings aren't very good. Pizza looks like it was made by a machine rather than a human. Too greasy, too much cheese, bland. This place would get one star from me if that was what this whole review was based on. But the cheesesteaks aren't too bad for a pizza shop. Not out of this world great, but like 3 stars. If we have someone staying with us from out of town and they want a steak and we sure as hell aren't going out in this weather/this time of night/whatever, City View is a perfectly fine. We order them occasionally and they are delivered quickly. So, it averages out to about 2 stars.
label: NEG

text: Beautiful hotel, and close to Bourbon Street, but awful service! I came here for a wedding and was helping the bridal party with last-minute details, and had such a difficult time working with the front desk, indoor staff and valet! The valet guys were impatient, rude, and not helpful at all. The front desk and indoor staff were also rude and impatient, and made things so difficult for us. The bridal party was spending a ton of money at this place and the LEAST the staff could have done was smile. They were awful! A pretty atmosphere is not worth the hassle of staying here. Plus, the restaurant food left much to be desired. Stay somewhere else!!

After picking out everything you need (I love that they have Mineral Agua there!) you are so psyched you got all of your needs in a one stop shop scenario and you head to the check out--here's where the games really begin. text: ** THIS REVIEW IS FOR THE SERVICE AND RESERVATIONS FOR LARGE GROUPS, NOT FOR THE FOOD. Food is good (4 stars), no complaints, but Tupelo gets 2 stars because I had issues with a large group reservation I made here. I made a reservation for 18 people to dine here after my graduation this past June, and reserved our table 6 months in advance. My graduation was to last from 4-6ish, so I made the reservation for 7. A week before the big day, my best friend's mom (also in our party) called to confirm. Everything was set. After graduating, we made our way to the restaurant, hungry and exhausted from the big day. When I gave my name the hostess said, "Oh, well your reservation was for 6:00, so we gave it away to a walk-in group at around 6:15 after assuming you weren't coming". I calmly explained to her that I'd known for an entire year that my graduation time was 4-6 PM, and there is NO WAY I would have reserved it for 6. I had even had professional invitations printed up with 7:00 as the time for dinner, and a member of the party had called and confirmed our reservation was at 7. She continued to argue with me and told me we'd just have to wait for the people who'd taken MY TABLE that I'd reserved 6 months before to finish before we could be seated to eat. My mother and I tried to change the situation, but to avoid making a scene we conceded and took my party (including my 86-yr-old grandmother, 83-yr-old great aunt, and 84-yr-old grandather) to wait at the bar until we could be seated at our table. Imagine my surprise when we sat at the bar and began chatting with the bartender, who revealed that they realized earlier that they had made a big mistake and mixed up my reservation time. Soo... that bitchy hostess just argued with me - a PAYING CUSTOMER, and the guest of honor - for 15 minutes when she knew the entire time I was right?!?!?!?! After waiting AN HOUR to be seated, it was 8 when we finally got to order. On my aging relatives' east coast time clock, that's 11 PM. Unacceptable. The meal was fine and we had no issues at all with our food. But while we were still eating and enjoying ourselves around 9:30, the waiters began clearing off out plates,turning off the music, brightening the lights and basically insinuating that they wanted to close and leave, so we should pay and go. I was offended by that because it was only due to their mistake that we were there so late to enjoy our meal. Don't trust this place for any important reservations or for large groups. They have certainly lost my business and I'll always remember this as the wrinkle in my perfect graduation weekend.

text: So, I have returned and I have tried SEVERAL more cocktails. I went on a Thursday, caiparinha night, and I have to say it was lackluster. Nowhere near as good as the ones at Rio Mar. Now here's the thing, I think they excel at drinks of the martini variety, as in ingredients that are shaken and then strained. Their drinks over ice are less impressive and I think it's party becasue of the large ice cubes they use. Now bear with me. I read this article a few weeks ago about this fancy new ice lots of bars are using. (http://www.nytimes.com/2010/12/01/dining/01shake.html?pagewanted=all) Apparently the cubes are prized because they are large, thereby chilling the drinks more quickly with less dilution. I think this is great for aforementioned shaken and strained drinks but not so good for drinks on the rocks. It makes the drink too icy and cold and you can't taste anything but the big ice block in your drink. So do yourself a favor and get the Faucheaux, which is tequila, basil and St Germain. Revelatory. Also fantastic was the Tru Kick, with Tru Gin, ginger syrup and peach bitters. Some of the best cocktails I've tasted on any fancy, signature cocktails list in the city.

text: I ate at Jazz a week ago, and was pleasantly surprised. I haven't ever been to New Orleans, but this place will give you the essence of being there in a Disney Land type of way. It was clean, and still had the new car smell. I give new restaurants a lot of lee way for service and food quality, but the day we showed up everything was fine. We ordered the chicken wings ($.50 each on Wednesdays), and considering myself a connoisseur of chicken wings, I was very happy with them! You can ask them to make them extra spicy, which is a good idea, as the regular are kinda wimpy. I wasn't in love with my entree, the Louisiana shrimp; it was too saucy with out a lot of substance. My rating was based on the skill of the deep fryer; he did an amazing job on everything that was deep fried. The wings, crawfish, catfish, shrimp and oysters were all cooked to perfection! Crisp and light, while still succulent on the inside. Keep that guy around Jazz! Be warned, with all new restaurants quality will vary as the chefs learn their stations... Long story short 3 out of 4 entrees were great, the appetizers during happy hour were $4.99 and worth every penny, the wings were fantastic and a great price at $.50 each on Wednesdays... and the place was clean with a decent staff. At my age with a 20 month old daughter I prefer the Disney Land Experience to the Bourbon Street experience, but your taste may vary (sorry no flashing from coeds while I was there)! The downers were my entree (the Louisiana Shrimp) and the bread you get when you arrive (big time blah).

text: They are right in between fast food and a sit down Burger joint in all aspects. Price, Decor, Quality of food. My review is rounded up, I'd really give them 3.5. You order at the counter just like a fast food joint, but they bring you your food to your table. The counter girls were friendly but sort of flustered (it was really busy). I had a mushroom swiss burger and it was quite large. I think I paid $5.95 for the combo with refillable drink + pouch of fries. The burger used real swiss, not processed cheese and the meat patty was quite hearty, probably 3x-4x the size of an IN-and-Out patty. The beef tasted fresh but was a little lacking in seasoning. It was cooked well, the bun soft and the cheese melted through, I did not care for the mushrooms. They use canned mushrooms, which I hate the texture of. I also wish the meat was cooked over a hotter surface as I like a crisp crust like In-and-out. The fries were thin cut and crispy, most likely prefrozen (they reminded me of McD's). Overall I think it was a decent meal, especially for under $6. My mates had the fried chicken sandwich combo and a bacon cheeseburger. I was told the chicken sandwich was tasty, but probably also a frozen and out of a bag. The bacon cheeseburger eater actually complained that his burger was too bacony! as if there could be such a thing. lol. Next time I'll try that, but I likely would not drive across town to do so. If I'm in the neighborhood it's cheap, fast, and filling.

text: Not their first rodeo, the Workingman's Friend has been around since the 1930s, and is still owned by the same family that built it back then. One of the best burgers in town (the ultra flat patties, as seen at Steak n Shake), gigantic cold draft beers (they have Bud and Bud Light, so you won't need to worry about making a decision), and a classic, nostalgic atmosphere, complete with jukebox, all add up to one of the most authentic experiences you can have at an American bar. The kitchen closes at 8pm, so you'll want to keep that in mind if you're looking to eat. They get a solid downtown lunch crowd, and you'd be surprised how many professionals frequent this otherwise-working-class establishment. They serve their beers in giant, frozen, glass mugs and they are cheap. On-site parking is plentiful, and it's fairly easy to find, though you'll want to map it online or on your PDA first. They also have a few cocktails to choose from, though I think it's a place to drink cold beer. But if you are feelin' a whiskey and coke, I ain't mad at ya!

text: Went to AnBrea's on Friday and wouldn't recommend it to anyone who values professionalism or their time. After I read the reviews on Yelp, I thought I'd give it a try. I have naturally curly shoulder-length biracial hair and needed a good cut badly. I called in the morning to make an appointment with Jamez for that afternoon at 4:30 pm. It was imperative I got my hair done that day-- if they couldn't do it, I would have gladly gone to someone else. I left work early, fought rush hour traffic and drove 30 minutes to get to the salon. When I got there, I was greeted by a receptionist at the front desk who acted as if I was a walk-in and said she'd, "see if Jamez can fit you in". She asked me if I wanted a "wash and curl" -- and when I asked her for clarification on exactly what that was, she smirked at me as if that was a ridiculous question. When Jamez, came over, he unapologetically told me that it was going to "be a while". I had to ask MULTIPLE times to drag out of him exactly what "a while" was. Finally, he told me it would be AT LEAST a two hour wait. He said he had other "standing appointments" and that I had been "lucky to even get an appointment at all". (Let's see: I had to leave work early, drove 30 minutes to be there ON TIME, was told to wait 2 hours and at this point it's too late to make an appointment anywhere else... I fail to see how this situation was "lucky" on my part.) He suggested that I have another stylist cut my hair. I asked him if that stylist was good with curly hair and he seemed to be offended by my question. He sarcastically responded, "all of our stylists are talented." I told him that I don't doubt that they are, yet still, not everyone can cut curly hair well. He just kept repeating the same line. Finally, he went in the back to talk to the stylist he wanted to do my hair. Guess what...turns out that she didn't know how to cut curly hair!!! The two of them then proceed to try to convince me to straighten out my hair! I told them that I wear my hair naturally, and they just kept on about how I should straighten it out for them, because it would be easier for them to cut. No doubt, they'd have charged me extra to straighten it too. Jamez then tried to get me to come back the next day for services. God knows how long I would have had to wait that time. This was the most unprofessional salon experience I've had in a looooong time. Their whole attitude is "you're lucky we're serving you." I can't stand this type of mentality amongst businesses. I left the salon stuck between a rock and a hard place, since I really needed my hair cut that day and it was now close to 5 pm. Wound up driving to the Hair Cuttery on City Ave, which was a HUGE risk on my part, but Tia, who works there took care of me, and actually gave me one of the best cuts I've had in years. All for $15, go figure. The only good thing about AnBrea's was that it lead me to Tia at the Hair Cuttery who gave me a great cut for less than 1/3 of the price. Absolutely wouldn't recommend AnBrea's to anyone.
label: NEG

text: My dogs love Country Haven Kennels. And for some reason I haven't figured out yet, Country Haven seems to love them. I first took my dogs to Country Haven last year. I had been using another kennel that took good care of them, but that kennel had this infuriating policy of a 2-day minimum charge, 3 on holidays, even if you had multiple dogs sharing a single run (they had a, I think, like 4% discount for the second dog: woo, don't spend it all in one place). I had finally had enough when I needed to board my 2 hounds for a single night in a single run for one night on a holiday weekend; their policies meant I'd be paying a very slightly discounted 6 night charge for the 1 run/1 night/2 dogs that I actually needed. And so I went shopping for a new kennel--one that wouldn't steal all my money with insane minimum-charge policies. I found Country Haven shortly after it had been sold to a new owner. Her name's Casey and she was clearly SO THRILLED to have this business, like it was her dream to be a kennel lady and it finally just came true. She also had a rescue dog or two who needed crash space chilling out at the kennel the first time I visited, and more or less every time I've been back since---I don't know where she finds them but she's clearly a big old softie where a homeless dog with a sad story is concerned. You can tell she really loves animals. She's always very sweet about mine, even though they're kind of hyper and loud and obnoxious: I adore them but I have to, they're mine, you know? Casey is always *very* good-natured about it when my dogs show up and make total asses of themselves... as they always do. One of my dogs has to get a bunch of different medicines or she breaks out in rashes, which is how I know she actually does get it when she goes to Country Haven. That's really important. And lastly, Casey's been really nice a couple of times about scheduling snafus. One time several months ago I boarded the huskies to spend a weekend in NYC: that weekend ended up being one of last winter's endless snowpocalypse dramas, and a delayed train home plus unplowed roads meant that I showed up to get the dogs like half an hour after the kennel was supposed to have closed. I can tell you for a fact, no one would have given me even 5 minutes of leeway at their old kennel. She didn't even charge us the "special arrangements" fee. And! Last month I boarded the dogs to go out of town for a week. On what was supposed to be my last night there, I got a phone call from a friend with an emergency, so instead of sleeping that last night, I was all Action Superhero Girl, and long story short, I slept right through Country Haven's evening hours when I was supposed to be picking my dogs up. I showed up the next morning as soon as they opened, and Casey was super chill about it, AND didn't charge me for the extra night, which is kind of amazing. So, you know. I'm a happy camper and so are the dogs. Only downside I can think of is that I got spoiled with the OCD levels of meticulous grooming at my last kennel---it's not quite as good at Country Haven. It's not enough of a thing to make a difference, though. And their weekend office hours are kind of limited, but it's kind of dumb to complain about that when, like I say, they're willing to make special arrangements for a fee that they didn't even charge me when they should have.
label: POS

text: My husband and I tried K-Paul's in New Orleans based on the rave reviews of a friend. One look at the gumbo they served me, and I couldn't help but wonder where in the world those rave reviews stemmed from. It wasn't the worst food I've ever had, but it definitely wasn't the best, and it wasn't real Cajun, if you ask me. I've had real gumbo, and K-Paul's didn't deliver that, not even at nearly twice the price of other restaurants in the area, serving the exact same thing. Where normal gumbo is lighter in texture, with a rue-based sauce/gravy, K-Paul's on the other hand was soupy. I could have saved myself $8.50 by spending 50 cents on a can of Campbell's File Gumbo soup, because with it's beef soup type base, that's what it resembled to me. I was so disappointed. As a girl with a Gram from the south, who grew up eating delicious gumbo, K-Paul's version definitely didn't measure up. My husband had the shrimp po boy, and while it was ok, I wouldn't say it was anything spectacular, or anything you can't get at any number of restaurants in the French Quarter, cheaper and tastier than the sandwiches served at K-Paul's. Meh. The highlight of the meal was the onion rings. Sliced very thin, with a tasty batter, they were delicious. The line at K-Paul's is a bit ridiculous, too. When you walk in the door, a staff member hands you a paper menu listing lunch choices. You then take a seat, peruse the menu, then get in a LONG line to place your order. I stood there for about 25 minutes or so, waiting to place mine. It's a bit chaotic, as the staff taking your order are also responsible for making drinks at the bar. Seems like things would run better if they had a designated bartender and a designated order taker? Either way, the ordering process isn't pleasant, especially considering the food that results, which was mediocre as best. Finally, if you plan to dine here and enjoy a soda with your meal, please make other plans. They charge $2 for one can of soda. At a restaurant like this, which is supposed to be somewhat upscale, you'd think they'd offer at least a fountain drink with free refills, but not here. I won't be back. All in all it was a big disappointment.
label: NEG

text: My girl and I were out to celebrate a little holiday romance. Dinner and a play were on call that night as my friend's play was showing on this rainy Friday night. We meandered our way through the St. Petersburg streets looking for a decent place to eat. Running out of options and time we decided Ai Mei was the best candidate available around St. Pete little theater. We were sore thinking about missing the all you can eat sushi - not all is lost. The night is young, my girl looks great, and Im hungry. We entered Ai Mei and were seated almost immediately. The decor was interesting. Wood paneled walls with a bamboo theme. It sounds cheesey but somehow they make it work. For those of you who love watching football while having california rolls, they have a big screen plasma in the place. Looks great. They also have a "Voted best in Tampa Bay - 2008" sign. I'd like to know who voted on this and what drugs they were on. Perhaps they should be more specific in what theyre the best at. We noticed we were limited on time - I asked our waitress if we could expedite our order and explained our need to rush. She took our order only to return and say the cook (I dont think he was a chef - please continue reading) only addressed each order on a first come, first serve basis so we'd have to wait our turn. I felt this was a dick move since you should at least humor me and tell me it would be rushed and cook my food as time allows. At the very least - please give me that. We started with some apps. My girlfriend ordered seaweed salad. Our waitress in training was unsure if they even carried it. She went to "check" and said they didnt. Later we found it on the menu. By then it was too late; my girlfriend went without an app. I got miso soup - I got it. It was your run of the mill soup. No complaints except for feeling like a jerk for eating in front of my hungry girlfriend. Finally, the food. I got the cashew beef. She got the curry shrimp. The portions were large and the dishes were hot. Plenty of food for the both of us. The beef was tender and the flavor was good. Nothing really stood out but I was satisfied. The shrimp curry was unacceptable. The shrimp were undercooked and felt flimsy and rubbery. While I wasnt expecting the freshest food - it should at least feel like food. I wouldnt trust Ai Mei for their sushi. Their food is ok, the experience is the same. Dont expect much from this place but it may be worth trying again if no other options are available. In the end, we made it to the play just in time. A good night all in all. Check out the pictures of our food. The presentation was good.
