text: Chifa was on the top of my list for Center City Sips. I absolutely love Sips because it's a great way to get an introduction to a restaurant without committing to spending a bunch of money. BUT at Chifa, I was denied the Sips experience. If I can say one thing about the service and general feel of this place it's MILITANT. As soon as I walked in, I got a spiel - "Sips is ONLY downstairs." In the basement. Where there's not nearly enough seating for everyone. The UPSTAIRS, mind you, is almost completely empty at 5:00 and I would think a newish restaurant could benefit from looking crowded upstairs where people outside can see. When my friends arrived, there was no seating and virtually nowhere to stand, so we decided to head upstairs and eat like civilized people with a table and space and service. The bartender gave us a hard time about ordering sips drinks and taking them upstairs. Lame. We go upstairs and ask for a table. The server says the table is only for the full menu - we accept these terms. At this point one friend has wandered off to make a phone call and the waitress says "You do have 3 people right." 3 seconds later "Where is your third person, does he know where you'll be." These servers need to CHILL! Finally, they take their food way too seriously. The server's description of the menu was right on, but quite a few times things were over explained. Honestly, though, I don't think it's the server's fault. It's the food's fault. One of the things we ordered was the Anticuchos. It was delicious, but the skewers basically came with 6 (yes, six) sauces - 3 on the side and 3 already on the meat. And it was about 12 pieces of meat total. That's totally overwhelming for any palate. Fun, but kind of pointless. The night was a blur of sauces and tastes and nothing particularly stood out accept the chimichurri. It was just too much on every dish. Also, when I order fries, I expect there to be a bunch, not just a handful. The rest of the night, we basically had to shoo the servers from taking our dishes prematurely and then we had the banana-pumpkin funnel cake. Sorry, but this dessert looked like a turd. I KNOW there have got to be classier ways to plate funnel cake. And it was greasy, not crispy. Definitely not worth $8. Finally, I can say I won't be going back here because I feel tricked. I wanted Sips, damn it. The restaurant knew that if people really wanted to stay, they would head upstairs and spend more money. But they could have just been nice about it and opened Sips to the whole restaurant. The people would have left by 7 or so anyway! Instead they made the Sips patrons feel lowly and acted really full of themselves. The upstairs really wasn't THAT special. At a restaurant, you don't get to treat your guests differently depending on what they order (especially when you are OFFERING things at a discount). I think Chifa could benefit from a slice of humble pie.
label: NEG

text: It had been quite a while since I had been to Catelli - and decided it would be great for Valentine's dinner. I was expecting a bit less because of the day-- but over all, especially in food department, they came thru shining. We check in and had about a 5 minute wait for our table - no big deal given it was Vday. Our waiter greeted us, noticing we had drinks already. He was very friendly and chatty - though for the rest of the evening, he seemed to always be about a step behind. They had a set limited menu for Vday -I knew that going in, but the selection was large and there were also 4 specials. I didn't have a problem finding something I wanted- and my guy was overwhelmed with the selection and specials. I started with a cream of wild mushroom soup which was completely delicious and he got the lobster bisque which he describe as 'like silk, wonderful'. We went on to apps- I am VERY particular about eggplant- so ordering the eggplant rolletine was a fence sitter, but WOW - done to perfection, I mean perfection. I rarely say that about eggplant. He got the seafood ravioli special as an app and loved every bite. For entrees he went with the veal chop, which he said was done perfectly and he didn't need a knife...served over lobster mash potatoes. I ordered the Ravioli in a pepper blush sauce, which comes with lump crab meat that I ask them to hold off (being a veg) they had no issue with that, in fact they brought it out on a separate plate so my hunny could enjoy it : ) The sauce was excellent and I enjoyed going in with the fresh baked bread to finish it off. The dessert tray came and was full of a ton of things I love... but at the waiter's suggestion I skipped the creme brulle, the crepes and the key lime tart and I went with banana bread pudding, since I love banana and bread pudding. We ordered coffee also -- which came right away - unlike our dessert. When it finally came, it was sadly our only food disappointment of the evening...all I could taste was cinnamon, fresh shaved cinnamon, but it took over the whole dessert. I could not get a taste of banana or creaminess that is usually in bread pudding thru the whole thing.. My second cup of coffee never came - and our waiter didn't realize it until after he brought our check, ran our card...etc.. So the waiter being off and the badly done dessert kept this from being a 5 star experience for me, but over all I truly enjoyed it.

text: Yes ! I think I have found my new hair home in Philadelphia. I heart the Alley but it's sometimes a pain for me to get out there and the Beehive is a relatively easy walk... How short in the back? How much length in the front? If I want to keep the length could she trim some of the feathery-fly-away ends? ("I'm afraid if I leave them alone you'll be back here in like a week because it's still too fuzzy.") Awesome. I like hair product as much as the next person, but almost every stylist I've ever seen has just used WAY too much gunk at the end of the cut. I end up walking out of the salon and wanting to go home to wash my hair immediately to get everything out. Not so here. I walked all the way home and when I took another look in the non-salon mirror, it looked exactly the way I would have done it myself. Amazing! text: Dear Rebecca S, The fact that you don't take SEPTA regularly means that you have very limited experience. If you need it to commute every day then you will discover how crappy it really can be. Have I had good experiences? Yes, a few. But they are far outweighed by the daily negative experiences which include: 1. Extremely dirty train cars-Spilled potato chips and potato chip bags, leftover wrappers, soda cans/bottles and spilled soda are de rigeur for SEPTA. Sprinkle in the odd leftover newspapers and fast food leftovers for garnish. 2. Extremely dirty train stations: City Hall routinely smells like piss. And to an extent many other stations smell bad as well. Not to mention the usual detritus ranging from digested sunflower seed husks/seeds spit out, cigarette butts, abandoned food wrappers, vomit, and other garbage. 3. Patron conduct-There's the people who sit in different aisles and yell at each other across the train. Then there's the cell phone breakup/relationship in termoil conversations, usually puncuated with loud swear words. Then there's the people that feel the need to share their love of X crappy artist on their crappy cell phone/portable radio speaker. Then there are the people that smoke in the train stations, despite numerous signs saying "Do Not Smoke". And the capper, those fellas who just can't wait and decide to whip it out and piss on the train platform. 4. Random train outages-This ranges from simple delays, which are to be expected to the full on "No trains are running past 19th St" announcement. 5. SEPTA customer service is uncaring and/or surly-They don't take change, even for low denomination bills even though at many stops there aren't token machines. They'll have conversations with fellow employees and travelers, letting you wait until they are good and ready to take your transfer. text: This place could have earned 4 stars if the owner/operator wouldn't have been so condescending. I ordered a $12.95 lunch special of Yellow-fin Tuna. My wife had the $10.95 Red Snapper special. The Yellow-fin had a few bones the size of toothpicks [NOT exaggerating] and tasted strong (dark stripe left in) AND it was dry. Wife's dish was fantastic: could NOT complain. Told the waiter who promptly told the owner. She came out with this set of lines: "All fish have bones." {This was SO insightful--who knew?} 'The dark meat is considered a delicacy" {this is why Trader Joes has this dark section of tuna part packed in tins labeled "Tuna for cats"} "If we were to remove all the bones the fish would be mush." {yes the old press-it-through-a-strainer method or the rip-it-apart-with-your-bare-hands method} Not anything like a sincere apology from this petite blondish woman in her late 40s. More like "I'm sorry you are such a fool. Let me see if I can pull the wool over your eyes. There ya go." But I thought I'd warn other Yelpers to steer clear of this place OR stand up for yourselves and make a scene. I was tired and not thinking straight or I would have made her eat one of the toothpick bones to see how she liked it. Update NOTE: I since learned that the fish was cut poorly across the back or bottom of the spine, which gave me the long toothpick bones that stiffen the fish dorsally and ventrally. These bones are NOT normally present in a properly done fillet--especially in tuna. So this place might SAY that it has a fresh fish market next to it, but that is no guarantee that they can cut it properly for their own dishes.

We split the Crudo Misto to start to celebrate our 1st wedding anniversary while staying at the four seasons for the weekend. The chilled crab claws were one of the most exciting things I've seen my wife eat. She absolutely loved them. They were a great size and came with an awesome hollendaise sauce. The oysters were the perfect size and quality and the tuna tartar was delicious. It could have been diced a little better as it was hard to split in a couple spots but still good. The second course was a little dicey at first but turned out to be great. We went with the waiters rec of Lobster Risotto and I got the Lamb Loin with Lamb ravioli. Unfortunately for my wife the Risotto came out with no flavor and was dry so the kitchen quickly remedied the situation and brought out our second choice. This vermicelli with pacific blue prawns was unbelievable. The manager came out and explained that the chef tasted the Risotto an admitted the other chef forgot a key component. My meal was cooked well and overall it didn't hurt the experience because we were having a great time and they took good care of us. We brought our own wine, 2005 Napa Silver Oak and it was delicious. They did charge a 25 dollar corkage fee which is a little high in my opinion but still better than buying the bottle from them. I guess overall there were a few mistakes for the type of restaurant that it is but it is still the four seasons and they will fix anything.

text: Just had lunch at Lola and I have to say I'm pretty disappointed - after all these great Yelp reviews I was expecting more. It's Thursday and the place was deserted when my friend and I got there just before noon. Only two other people came in while we were dining. The waitress was pleasant and gave us plenty of time to decide, and there looks like a ton of great things on their menu. It's pretty hot & humid so I decided against the lobster corn dog w/mac & cheese, which was what really intrigued me. Instead, I got a sandwich - the Medusa: spinach & feta spread, muenster, mozzarella, white cheddar and roasted tomato on sourdough. Plus a side of frittes. My friend ordered Antoinette: strip steak, gruyere, onions & mushrooms. "Roasted tomatoes" says something to me other than "sliced romas," which is what was on the sandwich. It pretty much tasted like a grilled cheese & tomato. Which isn't bad, but I was thinking there'd be more green on it from the spinach spread. It was way too cheesy for my taste, though it was definitely a tasty grilled cheese sandwich. The fries were warm when they came out but cooled quickly; my beef with any restaurant that serves fries is that they should be served in a cone like Belgians do, so they stay hot. Not Lola's fault that we're not in Europe, I suppose, though a good idea should be cross-cultural. They were definitely homemade and had the slightly greasy consistency of really good homemade fries. Quite tasty. The bread was fresh and grilled just right - very tasty bread. Jay's sandwich was a big disappointment: The meat was tough and one piece of it was half gristle! No one wants to dismantle a sandwich to cut off the gristle & then reassemble. Blech. Why serve that? It wasn't that it was bad, but for the price & all the good reviews the place has gotten I just expected more. If someone suggests Lola in the future, I'll go and try something different - maybe a crepe, since that's why Jay loves the place and that's what he usually gets. But I won't be craving it between now & then.

text: I'm all about a bargain and a $6 ticket for a matinee is great. I recently went to see a new release at the Roxy and I knew what I was getting myself into. The ceiling was caved in from water damage in several areas, the seats in the row I sat in were only partially anchored into the ground, and the row in front of us was resting on our legs. It was cool to have that roller coaster effect of being strapped down while watching the movie, but it does get tiring on the knees during a two hour film. The sound was stereo at best with defunct surround sound speakers hanging on for their life on the walls. The projection screen was minuscule. I've been to some old school theaters before, but this was ridiculous. About the only good thing I can add is that the reel switchover mechanism didn't fail and the movie went from start to finish without a hitch. text: Food ranged from great to meh. The matsutake soup was delicious, the best thing we ordered. The gnocchi were also delicious, but come on, anything drowned in that much truffle and cream is bound to be amazing. The egg-cup thing was a bit silly and rather tasteless. After asking for glasses of water upon sitting down, no one offered us any chance to look at the wine list. When we did ask for recommendations on pairings, the server was thorough in his description of what we might like. "You know New Zealand wines, of course, and this Pinot comes from the southern island, right up near that pass, you know, that's between [Town X] and [Town Y]? You get the morning mist rolling in off the ocean and then the evening fog cooling everything off, and that just brings out a lovely fruitiness of blah blah blah blah blah." He was SO pretentious. Even the water boy was haughty. Dishes came out fast, which felt, in this atmosphere, like they were trying to hasten our exit. The pieds de veau/sweetbreads were delicious. The pasta was very al dente and might have been good if it wasn't so thick. Not a delicate pasta at all. The wild boar ragout was ok, but we'd been eating pork all weekend at a wedding at Cochon, and nothing else can really stand up to the Stryjewski/Link restaurant. I ordered the apple dessert - cafe calvos - which was a clunker. Boring. The nougatine with salted toffy ice cream was much better, but you have to like really salty ice cream. All in all, we won't be going back anytime soon. Plenty of other delicious and less snobby/stuffy places to eat in New Orleans!

text: I came here in May of 2007, however, since I listed it as my "last meal on earth", I only thought it fair to write a review. A friend I was visiting in Philly suggested that we dine here one evening. I had no idea what to expect, but as a Francophile, I was excited to indulge in a classical French degustation menu. So the four of us enter the exquisite Parisian salon which consists of 2 floors, completely candle-lit tables, chandeliers, and a fireplace. I'm a sucker for an intimate, romantic ambiance so I already like this place upon first sight. I don't remember exact details, however I am reminded of the impeccable service which included a team of waiters who tended to the four of us in synchronized gestures. For each dish that was presented, they would lay the covered silver platters in front of us, and simultaneously lift the covers to expose an art display of French cuisine. The team of waiters would also walk together in a uniform line to/from the kitchen. At one point, I excused myself to use the restroom, and "my waiter" lifted my napkin off my lap, set it on the table, and walked me to the restroom... and if that wasn't enough, he patiently waited right outside the door! I still remember coming out of the restroom, a shock of surprise filling my every emotion, and then thinking, "what if I was in there for a really long time doing you know what?" He then walked me back to our table, pulled out my seat, and set the napkin back on my lap. Okay, so the FOOD... OMG!!! French orgasmic... to say the least! The dining experience here involves a prix fixe dinner of either a 6 course menu or 10 course menu written in French. I am now just recalling the foie gras with black truffle sauce and it's buttery consistency just melting in my mouth! Yummm! After dinner, the waiters rolled out a cart with an array of cheeses. One of the wonderful things about this place was that one of the members of our party is vegan and my fiance doesn't eat red meat... yet the chef catered to them with specially prepared dishes. Oh, and the DESSERT!!! When that famous all-you-can-eat dessert cart rolled out... I had to grip onto the arms of my chair to prevent myself from doing the "happy-dessert dance". It really is "all you can eat"... meaning you can sample as many beautifully-created tarts and fluffy cakes as you want! Then you are romanced with a platter of petit fours!!! I felt like Marie Antoinette surrounded by Alice in Wonderland pastries! I was in heaven! Complètement magnifique! A couple of things to note: Some might say the dress code is business casual... but I would lean towards the dressy/formal side. There are so many cougars in this place you feel like you are at a zoo. The dining experience can extend to some hours so prepare for a late night there. If you are comfortable spending money on fine dining, then you will have no problem when the bill comes. Some say it's overpriced, too expensive... but let's admit - it's all relative. (For the four of us, our bill was just over $800, excluding tip. However, we ordered cocktails to begin the night as oppose to a bottle of wine or two, so prepare for a more expensive check if you're ordering wine.)
label: POS

text: Meh. I've been to the Manayunk Hikaru for lunch and dinner and their sushi (while attractive) has always tasted below average. text: "There is nothing to fear except fear itself." That and shady food trucks/tents in Tucson, right? I saw a crowd of people at Topete's, and I sat down. I was served this amazing salsa in a squeeze bottle - I asked what was in it because it was so good. Of course, tomatoes, chili, garlic, and cilantro. But yet, there was something unique about it. I was given a menu in English, and I ordered the fish taco and breaded shrimp taco. They did not have ceviche. Boo. I got my order fairly quickly, and WOW, the fish taco was amazing. It reminded me of Rubio's except 130% better. I loved it. I did not even need any extra hot sauce because it was so delicious. The breaded shrimp (shaka) taco was good too. It looked like the breaded fish and almost as good. As I was sitting down, I noticed other people drinking these drinks that looked like Clamato with pieces of octopus in it. Also, there was a stone bowl that had chili, fruit, and tons of fresh seafood in it. I would say that tacos were equally as popular in selection as the mixed seafood. My total order was $7, and I had my order taken and ate my food within 10 minutes. It took about 30 minutes to get my check, but I was busy staring at other people's food anyway and sipping my Mexican Coca-Cola. I kept seeing signs for "bichi" and I'm pretty sure it's the vichy drink - it looks like V8 with swirly seafood in it. What are some other random things they say they offer? Dorado - dolphin (I really hoped not, but maynard assured me that dorado is a dolphin-safe fish and I think maybe it's mahi-mahi - thanks maynard!) Filete light - light fillets? Agsajos - Mexican hot chocolate Pulpo - octopus Definitely order the tacos. If you don't like fried foods, order the tacos gobernador (shrimp fajita like tacos), the campechana (seafood cocktail), molcajete coctail, and the cahuamanta (soup). You will also get a side of saladitas (Mexican saltines). Have fun!

text: (review in a nutshell: he came out for estimate, then I never heard from him again despite several phone calls and messages left) I was really excited when I saw all these great reviews, I thought finally I've found a great plumber! text: So we did two over/unders before going to this restaurant: average age (52) and number of people in here (10). Both were wrong. We waited three times as long as anyone should be asked to wait for just about everything. Soda refills, ordering, getting the check... the only thing that kept me from being obnoxious about it on the spot was that this woman seemed so confused about everything that it just seemed like it would be mean to complain the way you would in a normal restaurant. Plus she would comment on everything in a weirdly excited way, telling us how good something was, which you expect if you ask for recommendations, but it was just so out of the blue it was very weird. Like for that one second a light bulb flipped on in her brain, and the rest of the time she was on auto pilot not tending to the table. Food: was fine. But they seemed to be out of everything. At 5:30 pm on a Saturday. WHAT? did the world come here for lunch? How are you out of all of this stuff? Worse, when they were out of something, she wouldn't come back to tell us, she would just bring something else. Which turned out to be okay, but who does that? The best part of the meal was dessert by far. If you are going to go in here, just order five apple strudels and call it a night. Atmosphere: At 5:30 pm on Saturday I think we hit the dinner rush. It was only getting less crowded as the evening moved forward. The decor is about what you expect, weird kitschy fox figurines and beer mugs with lids, etc. Also a bit of just old decor, not German per say, just stuff your grandmother would have hanging. But it was decorated for St Patricks Day, a nice clash to the rest. Overall, this place is too weird. I am not intimately familiar with German food, and maybe this is the only place to get it, but I am not really sure how this place stays in business. text: The expansion of Tiffin into the airy, bright Tiffin Etc. (same entrance) is a welcome development. The separate, easy to navigate menu, consisting of four equal parts (Signature Pizza, Stuffed Parathas, Kati Rolls, and Beverages) offers distinctly different options from its sibling next door. While I understand the restaurant's eagerness to include the ubiquitous pizza option, I liked the parathas and kati rolls better. The spices and herbs in the Masala Aloo made the freshly fried potatoes come alive Stuffed wheatbreads (parathas) were distinctive depending on the filling - we liked lamb with cilantro and chilies and the marinated onion and herbs versions). What is really unique are the beverages. For the less adventurous, Thandai (almond flavored milk with fennel and rose) and the Nimbu Pani lemonade will make addictive companions to the food, the Jal Jeera, a drink described as "Cumin,lemon, and black salt infused cooler" will, admittedly, take a bit to get used to (I began to really like it about half-way through). With the intensity of what seemed to be freshly pureed seaweed (earthy and very salty), this drink is really a very different beverage. As for the pizzas: I have no complaints except that boredom creeps in when the hunger pangs are satisfied, I preferred eating the whole wheat flatbread parathas. The bill is easy on the wallet, the people at Tiffin could not be nicer, a really tasty and excellent lunch experience.

text: So i have been wanting to try this place for a long time! We went on a Friday night at about 7:00. It was pretty busy but there was space for two at the bar. The mood/scene is unlike any other micro-brew that I have ever seen. Usually there is a standard theme and darkness in them. This one just seemed like a place that found magical recipes for excellent beer and decided to just make a fun environment to serve them in. We took the advise and tried the pizza. Our waitress/bartender recommended the barbecue chicken. We also ordered some sweet potato fries as an appetizer. I have never been given this large of a serving of sweet potato fries in my life. And they were simply perfect. The pizza took a while longer to make, but was well worth it. I don't know what goes into the barbecue sauce, but I know they make it fresh in house. It nailed this pizza into one of my favorite pizzas ever. Our waitress was super nice and by the end had invited me to go out on a pub crawl this upcoming weekend. Apparently there are 50-60 getting together and riding bikes around the city to the microbreweries! Her name was Danni (guessing on spelling) and I would highly recommend sitting in her section. The beer....wowowow...I love trying micros...I also enjoy getting the samplers that each produce and trying a little of each. I fell in lust with the espresso beer...Yea, that's right, espresso...the aftertaste was just that...The only let down was that I really wanted to get a growler of it to go and they wouldn't sell it since it was a fresh made batch and high gravity....booo....fail... As for the environment...the outside looks like a sweet brick building...inside is just a concrete floor stuffed tables...there is random music playing...mostly random hiphop and dance types of music...my guess is the staff setup the playlist...i was fine with this since it was enjoyable music...not too loud...and they were all happier dancing and singing around...happier waitstaff equals happier customers...the most classic moment was sipping down some high alcohol espresso beer at a new microbrewery and hearing the thong song coming on...priceless i even decided to go back the following sunday just for a espresso beer and to try the homemade chocolate mousse (they were out of it friday)...but they are closed on sundays...blah...just an fyi

text: Okay, so after reading the other reviews I was ready for a pleasant experience. Wrong. I went here last night with my boyfriend hoping to find a cool, hipster (as reviews have mentioned) crowd enjoying after dinner drinks and food. It was a Friday night at about 7:30. What I found instead were a few couples here and there, and an abundance of groups in their 50s and 60s. Not a problem except that I would expect them to be somewhere nicer than this little place which isn't really sure if it's a hip bar or a shoddy restaurant. We sat at the bar as there weren't any tables available, which was just fine with me. The first thing I noticed was how long it took any of the bartenders to even notice us. It wasn't so packed where there were people standing or crowded at the bar. We finally received our menus and I have to say they're very creative in using old hardback book covers as their menu covers. Cool touch. I also thought their cocktail list was really creative and extensive, too. Not bad. I ordered the River Des Peres (dirty martini with kalamata olives) and it was very smooth. So far so good. I ordered the Lactose Insatiable pizzetta and my boyfriend the Mediterranean Chicken Pita. My pizza was good but how can you go wrong with Goat cheese, Feta cheese, and about 3 other cheeses on a crust. Yumm. My boyfriend, on the other hand, was served the most horrible mediterranean pita I've ever tasted. The pita was burned black on all the edges and the chicken was cold. Not cold as in it had cooled off from the grill, cold as in Tyson pre-cooked chicken strips from the refrigerator to serve on salads, cold! The Tatziki sauce was sweet when it shouldn't have been. He didn't even eat half of it. The cucumber salad side had no vinegar or flavoring. Awful. Last but not least, knowing that this is not a rowdy bar but rather that everyonre is eating at the bar, maybe they shouldn't forcefully throw all the plates and cutlery into a bin right next to the patrons. I jumped two times in my barstool. The servers and bartenders show really poor service skills and seem almost haughty. I guess if you really need to try one of the cocktails because you simply can't find it anywhere else then enjoy, but the vibe was dull, the food was bad, and the service had attitude. Not so great...

text: Being a big fan of Chef Stern's Gayle, I was anxious to see what he had cooked up at R2L, especially after being disappointed by his efforts at the erstwhile Rae and the current Midatlantic. The bar staff was friendly albeit still learning, we had to go with plain martinis versus an aviation, of which they hadn't heard. text: So far, Woodlands is my favorite Indian restaurant in Nashville. I'm used to only having two or three vegetarian options to choose from when I eat out, so Woodlands was a welcome change. The service is good, and the two dishes and the naan we ordered were all so tasty that I wished they didnt' fill me up so quickly. Woodlands' prices are also lower than the average Indian restaurant, which is a plus, especially since you're still getting a high quality meal. I'd recommend trying to gulab jamman for desert - warm, doughy fried cheese balls soaked in sweet rose water, mmmmm. Other reviewers have criticized Woodlands' decor, but I think it has an appealingly quirky and interesting look, compared to the more proper Indian restaurants I've visited. The one drawback to Woodlands is that if your date is a steadfast omnivore, you'll have to go elsewhere.

text: They have authentic Mexican food at a very, very reasonable price. For the win. - Large variety of meats, including tongue, pork, beef, chicken, etc. - They give you some wonderful salsa that's quite spicy, and one that's rather limey, along with pickled vegetables and fresh radishes. - One burrito is big enough for 2 meals or two people Nays: - It's small. Keep in mind, though, that this is NOT Tex-Mex, it's real Mexican.

text: As if it weren't enough that he is one of my favorite American writers, the fact that the owner maintains the home in its original form (except the living room where the bookshop is) boggles me. text: Please pardon the delay in this review - my bike purchase date was actually in 2008 but I have found the degree of service, personal attention and courtesy to be just as effective now as then. One the bike was selected, the manager spent 40 minutes getting the bike and I dialed. I'm not sure if this is always included or because he was having a good day, but it was def. appreciated. They did not push needless accessories one, and several times suggest I try other less expensive options when it comes to helmets, computers, etc. I have walked into the shop for an 'express tune-up' and I am out the door in 15 minutes flat. The staff remember your name and in my experience will always take the time to ensure you walk away from the store informed and comfortable with whatever it is you decided to, or not to purchase. text: This is really a sad, dying mall. I have visited the mall for about 10 years since my parents retired to the area. Even the worst malls in Orlando are better than this one. I had a long, luxurious 90 minute aroma-therapy massage (Swedish with a bit more pressure just where my back needed it) and hand-selected citrus and lavender essential oils. There are over 40 oils you can pick from and they'll blend you up a customized synergy for your treatment. Nice touch. BLISS. The waiting area was spacious - and even though there were 6 (yes, six) people waiting for 10 AM appointments on a Sunday, it was quiet and calm. One lady was wearing a robe (she was having a facial, I guess) but the rest of the 5 of us "lowly" massage clients just sat in our regular clothes. They also sell Yeah-Baby slippers - which are super comfy. The spa uses Yon-Ka skin care products and carries a nicely stocked array of aromatherpy products, candles and gift items. The owner (Jeff?) seemed cordial and the boutique person/receptionist (Stacy? Stephanie?) was very welcoming. I will come back for a SERIES (Saves you $10 - $30 depending on the series you pick) of treatments next time. The beef is low-quality, the buns are of the potato variety, and the fries dont come with some fancy malt vinegar sauce on the side. Which is to say- perfect. text: This place used to be better - I've been going to Nature's Food Patch for several years, its right down the street from my work and incredibly convenient. Unfortunately I've seen the store slowly declining in its quality and with the competition that has opened across the bay (Wild Oats and soon the Publix Greenwise marketplace) I find my visits less and less frequent. While I try to support the smaller, longer standing institutions even when the competition is priced less, I'm just repeatedly dissapointed with the direction this place has headed. I'm a vegan so shopping at a natural food store is pretty much a requirement to a well-rounded cupboard. Their grocery section is very adequate and actually priced quite reasonably when compared to other small natural food stores or even the big chains. I have, however, run into a frequent problem of purchasing vegan 'dairy' items and find that they are spoiled. This has happened to me on several occasions when purchasing fake cheese products, many of which were not even close to their expiration date, which leads me to believe that they may be improperly storing some of the food items that require refrigeration. For this reason I only buy dry good from them now. As for the deli, they made several improvements over the past few months but the quality and convenience has actually declined. To start off with the good, they do now have a hot food section which is great for lunch. No more bringing back cold lunches or having to reheat your meals in the company microwave! Also, they've expanded their racks to provide prepackaged foods from the deli cases including their pasta salads, tofu, and even sandwiches and wraps. Unfortunately, when they expanded the cases they did away with the convenient name tags that said whether or not items were Omnivore, Vegetarian, or Vegan. So now you have to ask the assistant behind the counter and the majority of the time wait while they scan the ingredients and give a not-so-helpful reply of, 'I think its vegan?" And while the prepackaged food is convenient so you do not have to stand in line... its been my recent experiences that prepared food in the deli has been suffering from quality controls that has lead to poor taste or even foreign objects in my wraps. Lastly, as someone whose been eating at the deli for several years, it would be nice if they brought in some new dishes for variety. To their credit, whenever I've had problems they've been very polite and offered to either exchange the item or offered me store credit. They seem sincere about improving the conditions but I see little change from visit to visit. When I shop here its for convenience and only for dry goods. Otherwise, I make a trip once or twice a month to Wild Oats and pickup a stockpile of my vegan essentials.

text: Mikitmoto's has been a Wilmington mainstay for sushi for about 10 years now. I went there once when it first opened. And while I always thought the sushi was very good the price has always kept me away. (For one of the best values in Wilmington, check out Niwano Hana formerly Mikasa). As a treat for our 9 year old daughter who absolutely loves sushi (and loves isn't a strong enough word here), we thought we would take her to someplace different than our usual mainstay and indulge her with some fine dining. Our visit was on an October Saturday night at 6pm. The dining room was fairly empty, however when we asked for a seat, the hostess asked if we had a reservation. When we replied that we had none, instead of telling us the dining room was booked, she said we should go check the lounge and see if there is a seat available. There's all of 4 tables in the lounge, all of which were full. At no point did the hostess bother to check for us. I though she was a little rude, but I'll forget about it for now. We were then offered seating at the large sushi bar which we accepted. As stated in previous reviews, the menu features a largely Asian fusion choice of fare among the wide variety of sushi and sashimi choices. Of course, our daughter gets the standard sushi platter. But my wife and I were in the mood for something different and both decided to order entrees. As a starter we ordered 3 different rolls which were all excellent. Our choices were decidedly on the spicy side and were not favored by our sushi-loving 9 year old, but we both enjoyed each one immensely. After this first round came the entrees. My wife ordered the Hawaiian Shrimp Stir Fry and I order Seafood Curry Stir Fry which was a special this night. Obviously, we are both fans of fiery food. I am also a big fan of curry and while I thought the chefs choice of adding chorizo to the Seafood Curry Stir Fry was an odd one, I was willing to give him/her the benefit of the doubt. The first thing I noticed was that my stir fry that was supposed to be served with rice was served with a thin noodle. But OK, I will roll with it. After my first bite, my meal was quite bland. Not at all what I expected from a curry stir fry. As my wife was eating I looked over and noticed that she kept dumping soy sauce on her meal. When I asked her why, it turns out that hers was also quite bland. I can appreciate the subtleties in flavor of a well cooked meal, but there was barely any flavor to be found this night. Now, preparation was spot on. The shrimp and scallops were cooked just right, not over-cooked at all. But the lack of ANY seasoning left me wanting for my daughters sushi platter instead. And as far as the chorizo? Well, it wasn't bad but....really out of place and added nothing at all to the entree. As for service, and after our less than stellar greeting at the door, our server was very attentive and never once left us wanting for anything. Great service from the waiter all evening. Mikimotos strong point is its execution of all sorts of sushi dishes. They do this very well. But if I am going to pay $100 for a meal for 3, and this included the one and only $9 mojito my wife ordered (my daughter and I drank water), I would expect a little bit more for my money. If you MUST go to Mikimotos, then I would say stick with the sushi. You won't be disappointed. But if you are looking for value for your money then I think you could do better. I'll give Mikimoto's 2 1/2 stars since Yelp only allows full stars, but 3 might be a little too much. Points deducted for our greeting by the hostess and for 2 pretty lousy entrees.

text: So being the gluttons for punishment that we are, my wife and I came here last night for dessert. We had just finished a fantastic meal at Miga at it was just to easy to cross the street to indulge my wife's chocolate craving. We were pleasantly surprised when we walked in the door and the place was actually open. No malfunctioning C3PO to rush us out. We were seated immediately in a dining room that reminded me of a tacky version of the Cheesecake Factory. Vats of chocolate, trite aphorisms on the walls, abstract drawings of some bald dude with an earring, references to Willie Wonka. . .I read somewhere that these restaurants belong in Disneyland or Vegas and I have to agree. So we decide to order the banana split waffle. It was very expensive -- $14 for a dessert -- but sounded delicious. The pictures on the menu made it look amazing (it was the one dessert they chose to showcase on the Waffles and Crepes section). But it SUCKED: 1. The waffle was one of the worst I've ever tasted. It was as if they took a week-old cake donut (not the Krispy Kreme kind, but the really heavy kind that crumbles), and shoved it into a waffle maker. The waffle was so hard that I needed a knife to cut it. And it tasted like, well, a re-baked week-old bad cake donut. The waffle we had at the Days Inn was a gazillion times better. 2. The chocolate was way too sweet, as if put too much sugar. Now I'm not a chocolate connoisseur, but I do know a few things about chocolate and I did take chemistry in high school. I know that high quality chocolates typically have a higher cocoa content. And from chemistry, if you increase the content of one ingredient, then the percentage allocated to the other ingredients goes down. So if the sugar content is very high (too sweet), then the cocoa content, by definition, will be low. So my conclusion: Max Brenner uses low quality chocolate. Unbelievable for a restaurant that bills itself as "changing the world's chocolate culture." 3. The banana was way over-ripe. Over-ripe to the point where it left a pungent aftertaste in mouth. 4. There was not nearly enough vanilla ice cream for this dessert. Ok, so maybe we didn't the amount of vanilla ice cream with the waitress (the menu just says "vanilla ice cream", with no indication of the unit of measure). But for a $14 dessert, most people would assume you'd get at least a scoop. We got something closer to a dollop. So there it is. I can't believe anyone could screw up a waffle, ice cream, fudge, and bananas that badly. Now that I think about it, there wasn't even any fudge - it was chocolate sauce. At any rate, this dessert SUCKED. It would suck even if it cost $3 in the "day-old" section of a bakery.

text: Things to love about a bar: 1) a great waitress who keeps your drinks coming 2) bathrooms, easy to access 3) dark areas, for seedy conversation 4) light areas, for light conversation 5) juke box, for the music of your choice. This place has all that, AND a grill cheese. Look no further. Plus, great location. I understand you can park in the ACME lot and no one cares? Just don't quote me on that one.
label: POS

text: Once upon a time, the pastrami on rye ( "Shane of the Selway") was my favorite sandwich. Today, I had the worse lunch imaginable - considering I spent $8 on 1/2 sandwich and cup of soup. This was not the same sandwich I became so fond of. There was more mayo and sauerkraut than pastrami.. In fact I'm not sure there actually *was* any pastrami.... The bread was so soggy from the mayo that I couldn't pick it up without it falling apart ( this was " easy on the mayo"???). The soup was so salty that I couldn't finish it. This is not the first time I've been disappointed by the food here, just the first time I've felt it was bad enough to warn others. Hopefully management will wake up and address the issue with food consistency....too bad. Not sure I'll be back.
label: NEG

text: Everytime I walked by this restaurant, I saw lots of people inside. Finally, I went in with my husband and tried their food. Maybe the food I ordered was not right. I ordered their curry chicken. I could say, I make much better curry chicken than they do. And they tried to refill my drink without telling me the refill was not free, and it would cost me 2 bucks more for a small milk tea. Another thing was they didn't give my change back which was about 3 bucks without asking me. Come on, do they have the rule to keep the change for their tips without asking? The food my husband got was a little bit better than mine. But I still wouldn't write home about that. One thing I noticed that, in this restaurant, it was always packed with much more Americans than real Asian people. If you want to eat true Chinese or Asian food in Chinatown, tell you a trick, don't go to the ones are packed with Americans, go to the ones packed with Chinese and other Asian people. This restaurant is not on my Chinatown visiting list anymore.
label: NEG

text: I've only been here once, but I was so overwhelmed that it was enough to last me a lifetime. I went with a group of friends on a Saturday night, and it took 5-10 minutes just to get in the door. Clearly, I expect bars to be crowded, but this was out of control. The place is so huge, you'd think that people would be spread out and have room to breathe, but that is a terribly wrong assumption. We managed to wriggle through the suffocating crowd, albeit very slowly, and headed upstairs hoping for a bit of a reprieve. It didn't come. I had to practically wrestle my way to the bar, which was about 3 deep at the time. When I finally got to the front of it, I had taken a few elbows to the head, and forgotten what half of my friends wanted to drink. Then, the bartender proceeded to ignore me for, not exaggerating here, 15 minutes. She just kept serving everyone around me, and just amazingly never managed to make eye contact with me. Finally, thinking that I had either passed out or gotten lost, a friend came to rescue me. Not even 30 seconds after he got to the bar, the bartender (who by this point I thought could be blind or at least lacking peripheral vision) came right over to take his order. Now, I've heard once or twice about this phenomenon where females don't like other females, but come on! How are you gonna just totally ignore a customer!? Terrible! I guess she thinks she just needs to work "the goods" for the guys, and fails to realize a chick here and there might need a drink.
label: NEG

text: Went here for the first time last week and was quite impressed. Very nice new park. The only reason it loses a star is because there really wasn't anything about it that totally stood out to me. It was just a REALLY nice Baseball stadium plain and simple. For example; San Fran has its location, Wrigley has the ivy and history, Millwaukee has the killer atmosphere. CBP is just really, really nice looking but that's about it. It's still high up on my list of Stadiums, it's just not the best. On another note; I loved the fans. The Phillies lost unfortunately, but the fans were as entertaining as an outsider would expect Philly fans to be.
label: POS

text: disappointing. maybe i wouldn't have been disappointed if i hadn't been under the impression it was going to be more like a farmers market, not basically just a bunch of long lines to a bunch of lunch trucks. i got there late, thinking it goes until 10 and my friends inform me that if the food hasn't run out, then it'll be an hour wait for me. no thanks. it had a lot of potential to be cool, there was music and i saw a lot of people i knew. but there was nothing to do but stand in line or stand around. meh.
label: NEG

text: Media Immersion room???? WTF??? I don't get this place, assigned seating, No student prices or daytime discounts, and nothing but Martin Lawrence or kids movies for some reason. I swear there was a summer where TWO Martin Lawrence movies were playing at the same time here. And one more thing, why oh why on earth do you have a bathroom attendant? I love stadium seating, it has that going and every now and then, it has a good movie playing..I'd hate to say it but it's likely the reason my girlfriend won't step foot into a cinema again.
label: NEG

text: Whoa, simmer down Jim G! Yes, Nimbus is good and it is a typical brewery/brew pub, spacious, warehouse-district, trains rumbling by every few minutes. Nevertheless, a great place to snag a seat on the porch (but not the horribly uncomfortable stools) and have a delicious microbrew. They have quite a few on tap and I believe you can do samplers to find your favorite flavor. A note on the service. It is laid back in a way that only brew pubs can get away with. I had very good service, but then again, I have a last name that bartenders often appreciate, so it helps.
label: POS

text: Great BBQ. Glad to see that Reno now has one. When ever we fly thru Dallas we always eat at Dickey's in the airport. Service is great and the customer service is outstanding. This will give the other BBQ's in town a run for their money.
label: POS

text: I FEAR the dentist. But maybe not anymore! I am a tooth grinder, and had worn down my front tooth so that eating, drinking, even breathing, was hurting last night. I called Dr. Anderson's office this morning, and they rushed me right in for a quick fix. Getting married this weekend with a huge toothache was NOT an option for me. The staff at this office were so accommodating and friendly..it was actually (I can't believe I am saying this) a PLEASURE to go here! My problem was taken care of lickety split in the gentlest, most attentive way possible. No wonder this office is popular for pediatric dentistry. I highly, highly, highly recommend Mid City Smiles!
label: POS

text: Oceanaire Seafood Room is probably my most favorite restaurant in Indianapolis. The seafood is flown in fresh daily and their menu options change with each visit, but I always get the chowder to start. I love the ala carte side options and my husband and I indulge in the asparagus and gratin potatoes with each meal. My favorite is the crab cakes and it is the only place in Indy I will get them. There aren't many options in a land locked state for good seafood and this place does EVERYTHING right. This is a great place for special occasions, b/c it is very expensive (we usually spend around $150+ with drinks every visit). It is SO worth it though!! :) The staff is experienced and well versed, polite and attentive. We celebrated our engagement and a couple of birthdays and we are always treated very well. Oftentimes, there are celebrity sightings as many of the local celebs like Peyton Manning enjoy it for a good meal out downtown. They are great about accommodating groups, and I love valet...which is only $7 and makes it very convenient in the winter. They have an amazing oyster bar as well if you are interested in that. Definitely must check it out! :)
label: POS

text: This is a cool place to hang late or have a late tex-mex dinner. The drinks and service are good. Lots of seating in-doors and out. I just got a salad, it was good, but i will definitely go back more hungry!
label: POS

text: When we first moved into the area 7 years we have been trying all of the local pizza delivery places trying to at least find one as good as the pizza parlor back home. I have finally found it at Xpress Pizza & Grill. Their pizza is crisp and thin and no grease unless you get the pepperoni and than its just alittle bit of grease just enough to slide your crust over yummmmmmm. They have the best wings I use to get my wings at Cannuli's but since they are no longer open they knock them out of the box. The wings are breaded and fried to order and than the buffalo sauce is smothered all over it. Their prices are very resonable. Yes its not a fancy pizza parlor it is a joint almost reminds me of South Street joints. Try them you won't regret it
label: POS

text: Worst dining experiance ever!!!! All the fish was super fishy, raw fish was all served warm (not chilled) and calamari was so over cooked it was like trying to chew a thick rubber band!!! Service wasn't much better. Servers didn't clear away old plates, and just dumped new plates on the table. Huge disappointment, there are many BETTER tapas places in town. We didn't finish our meal, and ate somewhere else. We were one of two tables seated on a weeknight (now I know why everyone was at the bar for various liquid nourishment). This is not worth your time.
label: NEG

text: The location is too small for the number of people allowed in. Forgetting Fire Marshal. And because there are only two TVs you have to strain your neck to watch whatever they'll tell you to watch. They rely on a cover charge for crowd control most nights, because it has gotten to be too popular of a place that they just have to turn away late arrivals at the door. Can't figure out what the fascination is. It's been an okay place to be if there's a big Flyers or Phils game and you are able to get in. I was not keen on paying a cover then not being able to see/hear the TV for most of the night. Food is decent. $10 daily specials menu is a nice addition. Better choices elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: I come here every so often cause it's never busy, and it's fast. super fast. and 24 hours. but the food, meh. it is what it is...diner food. and certainly not the best. but there's not much else you can get in the way of pancakes late at night in center city other than little Petes which is smaller and a little overcrowded at times. prices are ...ok. $6.35 for 3 pancakes and 2 eggs. guess that's pretty normal. the wait staff is nice enough, they don intentionally rush you. they give you your food so fast and then hand you the bill like they need a fast turnover and really...like i said it's never busy in here.
label: NEG

text: This library is to die for. It's every nerd's dream. I walked in through the main entrance which kept the old facade and you get that old clubhouse library feel. Then it opens into the renovated portion, which is airy and grand. I'm pretty impressed - they had a ton of computers for ppl to use in the labs, lots of seating (where some ppl took naps), and great wide study tables next to the glass windows on each floor. Content wise, I was pleased to see that they had international newspapers and well developed sections. I'm definitely taking my parents when they come to visit!
label: POS

text: Insanity is defined by doing the same thing repeatedly and expecting a different result. I have been to this place three times hoping for better and it hasn't happened yet. I LOVE buffets, especially Chinese, and I'm not very hard to please. I liked cafeteria food in school for pete's sake. This place just hasn't done it for me yet though. They do have a lot of selection, which is why I gave it 2 instead of 1 star. The last time I went, one of the warmers was either broken or not turned on so everything in that section was luke warm. Nothing like cold chow-mein, beef broccoli, and pot-stickers. Everything else I had was edible but nothing to write home about. I actually laughed out loud when I was trying to eat a piece of sushi trying to figure out what the gray matter inside it was so I opened it up the rice a bit to find, wait for it .........., canned tuna, yes canned tuna as the fish inside it. I finished up shortly after that and waved bon voyage for at least another year until my sanity leaves me again.....
label: NEG

text: Love it how some of these reviews are from the people that work there! Ha! Well, here's the deal-This place is way overpriced. I had some guy cut my hair that looked like he was 12. I said over and over and over again~DO Not take a razor to my hair! Did he listen? Nope. I went back to have my hair put into an updo-I even took pictures-The girl had no clue as to what she was doing. We paid a crazy amount of money for something one of my girldfriends could have done. I can't say that the staff was friendly, if I wanted that kind of treatment I would go downtown. Funny how this place is in far Norhteast Philly and they act like it's a high class establishment. It's too expensive for the kind of service they offer. No. I would never go back.
label: NEG

text: I was excited when I heard there would be a new micro brew in the Nashville area. I put it off for a long time, for the simple fact is I never have any other need to go to Cool Springs, and I still don't! The server was really nice, the pizza was average, and the ambiance was there. However, I can get that at a hundred places in Nashville. It just comes down to the beer isn't that good. I tried the porter first, and I was okay with it, not worth the 20 mile drive from Nashville. We then tried the pale ales, the IPA tasted metallic, and the red was under carbonated (which the waitress warned us about, so our bad on that one). We brought a growler with the intention of taking some home for a night cap, but we just stopped for a sixer on the way home instead. If I lived in the Franklin area I would probably go there, but I am happy with my Blackstone and Bosco's in town.
label: NEG

text: Stopped by the Palace at Ben before a friends wedding reception in Philly. This place is super cool (in the lobby of the Ben Franklin--which was a ritzy hotel back in the day but now is upscale apartments). The drinks are stiff and the appetizers are great. We had the fried potato balls stuffed with cheese and spices and one of their specialty breads. I definitely want to come here again if in town for business or leisure. One things for sure, late night after the wedding I'm getting a famous cheese steak. Woot Woot.
label: POS

text: After hearing positive reviews, a gift card was purchased for a family party and lost. The staff and manager of Parc Bistro refused to reissue or offer any accommodations to our unfortunate situation, even with gift card purchases available on record. I can understand that a policy is a policy but find the way it was dealt with over the phone to be very unprofessional and with a hint of arrogance. Enjoy what this place has to offer, but should you ever need a favor--don't count on it from this place.
label: NEG

text: Ok, so Peace A Pizza does have a large selection to choose from, but I feel the pizza itself is largely overrated. Every time I decide to give PAP a try I am let down. In my experiences the pizza seems like it has been sitting out for hours, and doesn't always taste like it was made in the same day. For my taste the pizza is doughy and heavy. Peace A Pizza hangs a hilarious sign on their door that reads "Sorry, we're Open" during business hours, well Peace A Pizza...me too...me too.
label: NEG

text: Let me start by saying that i LOVE BBQ. I could eat Ribs any day of the week. But, I probably would never order them from Percy street BBQ. They were practically flavorless, although cooked to an appropriate temperature. My friend and I both ordered the double down, had the ribs, chicken, and brisket (the brisket being the absolute winner). I love eating crispy chicken skin, and I couldn't even stomach a few bites of the chicken; it had a very rubbery consistency. I was intrigued by the Root Beer Chili, and was sadly disappointed (not to mention it was luke warm at the very most). Beer choices were good, but I didn't want to eat at Percy Street because of the alcohol. Dessert, however, made the experience. The Pecan Pie was heavenly! Banana Pudding was really thick, but tasty nonetheless. Service, however, was awful. Our server was aloof and inattentive. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted rather awkwardly by a manager. I can justify a sort of absent minded server when a restaurant is busy, but i can't when there are literally two other tables seated in the restaurant who are on dessert. There are a bunch of simple things that should be done during service that weren't. And from working in a restaurant, i understand how those little things can either make or break an experience. I was disappointed in the food and service enough that I don't have the desire to return for seconds. And i never say no to seconds when it comes to BBQ.
label: NEG

text: I have to say that if you were to judge a book by the cover, then this is the place to be. It has a great atmosphere. I love the windows and the second level (it allows for an open breeze experience). Overall, I will say that the service is the pits. Maybe they are still getting the hang of things; however, my friend and I waited about 30 minutes for the waiter to bring our drink from the bar. That was just crazy. The wait staff is "too quick" to provide you with a good experience. I may thy this place again; however, I will certainly wait until it has been open for a few months and their service improves.
label: NEG

text: It was crazy busy the night I was here. I believe there were only four waitresses for the entire room. Our waitress was great but VERY busy. My Oysters Desire were awesome as was the crawfish etoufee. Stay away from the shrimp creole. It was bland and tasted canned. They use A LOT of garlic so be prepared with some gum or mints for later in the evening.
label: POS

text: This small country kitchen located in the heart of Trevose looks outdated, but packs a punch with home cooked meals. The menu has traditional German cuisine like schnitzel. I had the Schnitzel Jaeger (red sauce, mushrooms, peppers, onions, bacon) and it was very tasty. Meals come with choice of two sides and I went with the spatula, and the sour kraut. The kraut was delicious, very well seasoned, and creamy, nothing like I've had before. The menu also has seafood, and more american style dishes which we did not try. The cost was very reasonable, it was only $20 bucks for two people. They take credit cards, but tips are cash only.
label: POS

text: I went on a weekday around 1:00PM. There was only one person working the counter and the food took about 20 minutes or so due to the large line. I ordered a vegetarian burrito and a side of chips and salsa. The burrito had fallen apart before I picked it up. The chips looked like store bought tostitos with canned salsa. There was nothing exceptional about either item except for the price, which was only slightly above Taco Bell prices. Given the slow service and the somewhat bland food, I find it hard to recommend Hot Tamales.
label: NEG

text: I like to drop in here whenever I'm in or near Santa Barbara. They often have great beer brewed in-house in a variety of styles, as well a bunch of other interesting beers on draught and in bottles. I recall that they offer growlers, so you can take a jug of their finest home with you, then bring it back for refills. The fish and chips is done nicely. Good beer-battered sea beasties done in a beach style, as opposed to the giant slabs of cod you get at a British pub. I get this every time I go, so I can't speak for the other items on the menu. Standard pub fare: appetizers, sandwiches, burgers, etc. The service has always been fast and attentive, and the booths are comfy enough. They do have those extra tall tables and chairs that I don't much care for, but whatever. Check them out if you're nearby. It's one of the more relaxed, casual places to chill in the area.
label: POS

text: After 2 visits to SOTR, I am not impressed. First of all, as other reviewers note...the place just has a funky smell to it. Drinks are over-priced, sushi is so-so, and the server asked if we needed anything every 3 minutes. We ordered vegetable tempura for an appetizer, and some of the pieces were still raw in the middle. We ordered some various nigiri and a few rolls for dinner. The fish pieces on the nigiri were the thinnest I have ever seen. We definitely don't see a reason to come back here; There are several great sushi options on the northside including Asaka, Naked Chopstix, and Wasabi...
label: NEG

text: Had a lovely meal at this cute little neighborhood BYOB a few months back when it was still warm enough to sit at the tables outside. The food is authentic and lovely: Try the anchovies and the papardelle with lamb ragu (this traditonal Italian dish--my hunch is that it's southern Italian because it's hearty and saucy--has been consistently popping up at homey trattorie for a few years now, but it's rare for me to see it with lamb and not boar). Great people watching as everyone is out and about, walking their dogs, pushing strollers, coming home with groceries. Wait staff is really friendly and knowledgeable, effusive about their food, and very Italian (but not in the leave you alone for so long you think they've forgot about you kinda way!) Can't wait to go back; I didn't order it but I'm intrigued by this Gnocchetti Armenville of which they speak. When can it be mine?
label: POS

text: I agree with the other review that said it wasn't real bubble tea. I didn't even see fruit tea options! My bubble tea didn't have much bubble...I don't think it had much tea either...I'm not ever sure they have a real shaker. I did go with milk tea. I ended up with ice chunks and the powder they used didn't seem to get mixed very well. It was genius to put this store in the mall, but maybe they should have skipped on the ice cream and soft drinks and invested a little more into their bubble tea. Do they even have tea at that store? The taste is not very good. I also recommend Fat Straw - it is way Awesome for all your bubble tea needs and it's very close to all the universities. I think their prices are better too, but I can't be 100% sure of that. This is no offense to Bubble Tea House, but I'd never buy their product again - even if I were desperate.
label: NEG

text: Last night I was in the mood for Vietnamese food - specifically a nice big bowl of pho - and we ended up Kien Giang. The food was OK, not great - and lacked some of the more complex flavors that I've experienced at other Vietnamese restaurants. But, this place is cheap - $5.50 for a bowl of pho, $2.00 for an order of 2 Vietnamese eggrolls, and $2.00 for a coke. The service was a little slow and there was a huge language barrier between the server and myself - ultimately, the numbered menu helped. I'd go back, but only if Miss Saigon was closed for the evening. One other potential issue is that they don't accept credit cards, so be sure to bring cash or your checkbook.
label: NEG

text: Sketch is probably the right name for this experience, that I wanted badly to feel but didn't. Hungover and needing the revitalizing hot beef and cheese injection experience, I was led astray into the sobering grunge of Fishtown in midday sun and felt worse for the wear pretty much across the board. The place is going for laid-back neighborhood vibe, but finishes a note too swarthy. Pros -Dipping sauce... it's just mayo in a variety of disguise but still delicious. -Old dog on the floor. -Crayons Cons -A burger too far - some inventions are too good to mess with. You don't need to reinvent the wheel, you can't build a better mousetrap. Same with burgers. Sketch got too high concept on the 'smashed onion burger' for example, and I paid the price with his huge mess. Unwieldy and over-complicated, it seemed all I could taste was cheese and burnt onion. Maybe that's someone's thing. Not mine. -Cheese - I never thought I'd say this, generally being a big fan, but when your entire enormous patty is covered in a half-inch thick layer of congealing pepperjack, it's a little off-putting. -Milkshake-down - big, undifferentiated soft-serve with a pump of coffee syrup for like $6.
label: NEG

text: I stopped with my 2 kids on a trip down the coast as we headed back to L.A. I wanted to have dinner at a nice restaurant that was kid-friendly. We sat outside in the pleasant patio. i was relieved to see 2 other families with young children also dining there. The kid menu was okay but not much effort put into it -- no printed menu or fanfare -- obviously not interested in families. The food was way above average but not stellar. I had the special cod and it was well prepared. My son had filet mignon and he enjoyed it. My daughter did not like her cheese sandwich since it was on sourdough bread. However, both enjoyed the vanilla ice cream for dessert. I was surprised how busy the restaurant considering it was a Tuesday night and felt they were understaffed. However, our waiter was pleasant and attempted to check on us more than a few times -- a surprise since he was busy so I tipped him well for just trying. The food did arrive timely and hot. Pleasant experience.
label: POS

text: Did not dig this place one bit. Soggy "panini", fake prosciutto, fishy calamari, dirty fryer, greasy wings, and poor bar service. Blah!
label: NEG

text: My consumption of butter chicken, naan, and cauliflower is but a blur of hand over fist shoveling into mouth. It is the best Indian food I've ever eaten. Five stars is almost an insult. High quality food, large portions, low prices, and occasional "extras" thrown in with your order (I received a side order of lentils which are out of this world). They will deliver in the traditional "tiffin" style for lunch or dinner, or you can order take out or dine in. It's worth the hike to Northern Liberties. I ordered one meat dish, one vegetarian dish, rice and naan. There was enough food for 2-3 meals. Everything is nicely labeled in the containers. And did I mention the delicious blend of savory goodness? I can't wait to go back. Maybe tomorrow. Edit: I did go back within a week and had the chicken tikka masala (I know I know not a real Indian dish like chop suey is to Chinese)-- IT WAS DELISH. GO NOW.
label: POS

text: ok i admit it I'm a sushi snob. I would gladly exchange all meals for sushi if I had a larger bank account and didn't fear acquiring mercury poisoining (Jeremy Piven style). So needless to say I was excited to try this place in light of the glowing reviews. The interior is tastefully decorated, although the music needs a major overhaul ( we left while being seranded to the sweet sounds of Bryan Adams). As far as the sushi goes it was just ok. The prices were a bit better than comparable sushi joints in the city. The portions were similar, but the fresh fish was lacking. The hamachi was tough and chewy and the accompanying sushi rice was also a bit tough. The specialty rolls were much better than the nigiri, but when you have spicy sauce and tempura flakes, its easier to mask that not so fresh fish. Service was a little slow and they forgot my miso :(. Overall a disappointing sushi outing.
label: NEG

text: It's worth going to once in awhile for variation, since there aren't really any other delis around the area, but it's more out of necessity than quality. The sandwiches (usually a reuben) are fine, but not really anything special. Because of their geographic monopoly, they can overprice everything, which I understand from a business perspective but still resent as a customer. Contrary to other yelpers, I think the service is fine. The staff is pretty talkative (in a nice way) and I appreciate that as I wait in line.
label: NEG

text: We tried the thin-crust cheese pizza, which was really just average. However, if you do try this place, look up right when you walk in - you'll see a dizzying steep staircase winding up to a lighthouse, pretty neat. Other than that, the pizza is just ok.
label: NEG

text: Wow, how can you screw up a salad? I mentioned to the salad-maker that I was not a fan of a lot of dressing but it didn't have to go on the side. So what's the main ingredient when I get it home? Yup. 2nd biggest ingredient: Granny Smith apple slices. Lots of dried cranberries too. Aren't these sort of supposed to be accompaniments? Also, the ringer asked what kind of roll did I want? Wheat/white? What kind did I get? Beans. Nuttin. I'll stick with Cosi.
label: NEG

text: Once you've been to one, you've been to 'em all, but this one sucked for more reasons than normal. 1)There was virtually no waiting area. There were chairs set off to the side in the walkway next to the salad bar, and only four of them and the entrance had two benches big enough for three people max on each. That was it. (The reason being a problem will show.) 2) They are severly short staffed in either the kitchen, with servers, and/or bussers. It took forever (10 minutes) to get drinks, it took about another 10 to take our order. It took another ten minutes to realize my glass had been empty for ten minutes and another ten minutes to get another drink. It took another 25 from when we ordered to get the food, but it did come out hot. When we decided to add something else to enjoy as well, that took another 25 minutes. Each table seemed to wait this long. On top of all that, their bussers were no where to be found. At first he cleaned off the three tables behind me of their plates, but didn't wipe them or take the trash. It took about a half hour to the busser to buss 3 tables. In the meantime, prime dinner wait time has started and people are upset because their five minute wait has turned into 25 minutes and their standing because there is no place to sit. 3) The servers are not professional. I don't mind if a server wants to hook me up with a discount or free desert, but don't ask me if I want to just include another persons full salad bar with my meal because it will be 2.99 vs 7.99. Just either say you're going to do it or don't do it because you've now put me in the position to say, "Yes, I'll steal from your employer by telling you to break some ethical rules." And where the hell were you to fill my drink that's been empty for 20 minutes? And how come there are no clean plates at the salad bar? And why do I have to sit next to unclean tables for a 1/2 hour? It's sad because this restaurant is only a couple years old, but they are run like a place that is pinching every penny, including getting more employees and cutting service, instead of an emphasis on service. What the owner of this restaurant doesn't get is that most people will pay for, and come back for, service. Eventually this location will run out of customers. I will not return to this location.

text: I really wanted to like Agave. I tried. But I just can't. It is a small place, and often so crowded you can't move. So, patrons stand around hawking tables and the second people get up from a table, those waiting sprint to get it before someone else does. I felt like we were stalking the poor folks at the table we wanted! Their food is just okay. The chips they brought out with the salsa were stale. We told our server and she brought us more, but they were only slightly better. I had the brisket enchiladas, and they were average at best. I ordered a side of black beans, which were kinda like mush. Didn't eat them. A few of my friends got various tapas and felt the same way. The food is not terrible, but I have no desire to go back. I also thought the prices were high for what you get. Agave does have a good bar. It's small and hard to get a drink if it's crowded, which it always is, but they have a great tequila selection. They also make creative, fruity concoctions which were fun. I'd be more apt to go back for just drinks than I would dinner. I'm still trying to give them time to work out the kinks. I hope they do.

text: Anyone who knows what over priced, over done and over hyped clothing stores and fashion look like will no doubt find evidence of it at any Blue Bee store (Blue Bee Jeans, Blue Beetle, Blue Bee shoes, ect.) The feeling, clothing and people this store it caters to shouts "I just moved from Dallas to Montecito, got lipo, and am now newly single after a very rewarding divorce" look. ---My bad, the lipo comes after the divorce, that's it. It is all too glittery, too "look at me, I'm wearing the same overpriced, low waist jeans my pre-pubescent daughter wore yesterday to grade school." 50 year olds and 12 year olds should not share the same wardrobe. But when they do, you'll no doubt find them shopping at Blue Bee. The staff of ALL Blue Bee stores are unnecessarily snobby and rather too proud of the crap they try to sell you. The majority of them don't know what interesting and/or flattering fashion is anyways. Just try admiring what they wear to work, and you will no doubt find nothing that in the least that entices the eye. I will argue that if you are looking for anti-sweatshop made standard tee shirts, hoodies and (some) jeans, (and are ready and willing to pay for this,) you will find them in a variety of shades and styles in Blue Bee stores. But I stress again, ignore the staff because they will ALWAYS find it necessary to sweetly remark that everything looks "super hot" or "sooooooooo, like, cute on you, omg," when you really just look like another poser or the next innocent fashion victim. Side note: Blue Bee is famous for having bi-annual, entire store sales that last 3 or more days, with discounts ranging from 50-80%, that many poor suckers will set a 5am alarm for and continue to stalk and camp outside the store until it opens. No hurt feelings intended, but the victims are usually Montecito mothers with nothing else to do but waste their time buying their undeserving, spoiled, teenage daughters new wardrobes every other weekend. You know, something to occupy all there free time. Anyone with half a brain would realize that in order to mark down an entire season's worth of clothing at such outstanding discounts the store has initially overpriced every thing you see more than what is retail norm. So it's really a big joke. Clothing stores only mark down stock that is not selling well and that could become another financial burden if not sold at all. When a store discounts clothes at such rates it usually means they are going out business, unless, like Blue Bee of course, they can still make a growing profit on all those suckers out there and even afford to do it every single passing season. So, please, take caution remember that you (your husband, your parents or maybe even your great grandparents) worked too hard for you to allow yourself to waste your cash in a place that doesn't even appreciate what it is worth.

text: I think the Mall portion of Legends is really well thought out and beautiful. I really like that they incorporated so many local and Nevada themed artworks. I'm not sure I understand everything and it's not entirely a cohesive look, but I do appreciate the well illuminated art installations. I really like the fish sculpture. I think they need more public restrooms, and more accessible ones. They have proper signage but the smallish restroom is located down a long dark isolated hallway in between the stores (the backdoor to many stores actually) and my friends deemed it the "rape corridor". I haven't been to many of the stores, but I'm glad to see that it's a mixed outlet and regular retail mall. (funny that they tore down an outlet mall to build another one on top of it, albeit a much better designed one). Of the few stores I've been in, the employees of the various retailers were very well trained, friendly, and helpful. The only store I went into was BCBG and while I did buy a great dress, I would say that I can usually find better deals on newer items at Macy's or Dillards on sale.
